target.title: fix(qa-lab): bound internal transport response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA Lab runs could buffer arbitrarily large internal adapter responses or remain stuck after response headers when a Crabline adapter or runtime-parity debug endpoint returned an oversized or stalled JSON body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both QA Lab-owned response readers now use the public plugin SDK response-limit seam with a 1 MiB cap, a 5-second idle deadline, and a 15-second overall body deadline. Crabline keeps failing the injection on invalid transport responses, while runtime parity keeps its existing fail-soft behavior and treats unavailable mock request data as absent; normal provider message IDs and parity ordering are unchanged.

## User Impact

QA operators get bounded failure instead of memory growth or an indefinitely stalled suite when an internal transport endpoint misbehaves. Healthy Telegram, Slack, Matrix, and runtime-parity responses continue through the same workflows.

## Evidence

AI-assisted.

### Real behavior proof

Environment: local Linux machine, Node `v24.18.0`, exact base `b8b064a9483ee0917648207ffe91438a2da8c828`. A real localhost HTTP server streamed either 2 MiB of JSON in 64 KiB chunks or sent a JSON prefix and then stalled. The harness loaded the production `postCrablineInbound` and `captureRuntimeParityCell` callers from an isolated main worktree and this branch. Main's private Crabline caller received a proof-only export in the isolated worktree; its implementation was unchanged.

Command (run once against main and once against this branch):

```text
node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-qa-response-proof.mjs \
  <worktree>/extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.ts \
  <worktree>/extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.ts
```

Before (`upstream/main`):

```json
{"surface":"crabline","mode":"oversized","outcome":"resolved","elapsedMs":240,"bytesWritten":2097166}
{"surface":"runtime-parity","mode":"oversized","outcome":"resolved","elapsedMs":223,"bytesWritten":2097166}
{"surface":"crabline","mode":"stalled","outcome":"observer-timeout","elapsedMs":6501,"bytesWritten":11}
{"surface":"runtime-parity","mode":"stalled","outcome":"observer-timeout","elapsedMs":6501,"bytesWritten":11}
```

Premise: both main callers consumed the complete 2 MiB response. After only 11 bytes of a stalled JSON body, neither caller completed within the harness's 6.5-second observer deadline; the guarded fetch had already resolved on headers.

After (this branch):

```json
{"surface":"crabline","mode":"oversized","outcome":"rejected:Crabline inbound response exceeds 1048576 bytes","elapsedMs":153,"bytesWritten":1114124}
{"surface":"runtime-parity","mode":"oversized","outcome":"resolved","elapsedMs":130,"bytesWritten":1048588}
{"surface":"crabline","mode":"stalled","outcome":"rejected:Media download stalled: no data received for 5000ms","elapsedMs":5005,"bytesWritten":11,"closedBeforeEnd":true}
{"surface":"runtime-parity","mode":"stalled","outcome":"resolved","elapsedMs":5004,"bytesWritten":11,"closedBeforeEnd":true}
```

The Crabline caller now fails at the byte/idle boundary. Runtime parity still resolves fail-soft, but stops reading at the same boundaries. Both stalled connections were canceled before the server ended the body.

Negative controls: the same production paths' existing healthy-response tests remained green, including normal Telegram/Slack/Matrix provider message IDs and normal runtime-parity request ordering.

```text
Finished in 27ms on 4 files using 7 threads.
```

target.title: fix(mattermost): validate channel id before send, fall back to name lookup when not found
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent uses the `message` tool to send to a Mattermost channel by name (e.g. `#finance`), the delivery system can pass the channel **name** directly as a `channel_id` to the Mattermost API. Since the Mattermost API expects a 26-character channel ID, sending a channel name causes **403 Forbidden**. This also silently poisons the delivery queue with entries that retry indefinitely.

**Root cause chain:**
1. `resolveMattermostOpaqueTarget` unconditionally returns `{ kind: "channel" }` for any 26-char bare input after user lookup fails — including transient 5xx/network errors where it should return `null` and defer to proper parsing.
2. `resolveTargetChannelId` returns `params.target.id` directly for `kind: "channel"` with no validation step — a non-existent or name-shaped id hits the API and gets 403.

## Evidence

### Targeted tests

All existing `parseMattermostTarget` tests continue to pass — channel name detection is unchanged:

| Input | Expected |
|-------|----------|
| `channel:finance` (non-ID) | `{ kind: "channel-name", name: "finance" }` |
| `#off-topic` | `{ kind: "channel-name", name: "off-topic" }` |
| `channel:#off-topic` | `{ kind: "channel-name", name: "off-topic" }` |
| `channel:dthcxgoxhifn3pwh65cut3ud3w` (26-char) | `{ kind: "channel", id }` |
| 404 user lookup fallback | returns `{ kind: "channel" }` for valid raw IDs |

### Fix coverage

The `send.test.ts` mock for `fetchMattermostChannel` resolves with the input channel id, simulating successful validation for the happy path. The catch block exercises the name-lookup fallback when validation fails.

**Fix 1 — `resolveTargetChannelId` (kind: "channel" path):**

When the target is classified as a channel id, the code now validates it exists via `fetchMattermostChannel`. If the channel is not found, it falls back to `resolveChannelIdByName` instead of passing the unresolved id directly to the API.

**Fix 2 — `resolveMattermostOpaqueTarget` (non-404 errors):**

Previously any user-lookup failure (including 5xx/network errors) classified bare 26-char inputs as channel ids. Now only explicit 404 responses return `kind: "channel"`; transient errors return `null` so callers fall through to `parseMattermostTarget` + `resolveTargetChannelId` validation.

### Test plan

- `send.test.ts`: Added `fetchMattermostChannel` mock that resolves with input channel id (simulating valid channel). The existing test for 404 user-lookup fallback exercises the validated channel-id path.
- `target-resolution.test.ts`: 404 fallback test unchanged — still returns `kind: "channel"` on explicit 404.

target.title: feat(onboarding): offer detected Claude Code/Codex/Hermes memory imports across CLI, macOS, and Linux onboarding
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users switching to OpenClaw from Claude Code, Codex, or Hermes already have memories on their machine, but onboarding never offered to bring them over. The memory-migration engine and the `migrations.memory.plan/apply` gateway RPCs existed, and the Control UI had a settings page, yet none of the onboarding flows (CLI wizard, guided CLI flow, macOS app, Linux companion app) surfaced them. Hermes additionally could not participate in memory-only import at all: its provider declared no `supportedItemKinds` and only emitted `append` actions, which the memory RPC rejects.

## Why This Change Was Made

One detection-gated "import your memories" page in every onboarding surface, reusing the existing reviewed engine:

- **Hermes memory-only support** (`extensions/migrate-hermes`): the provider now declares `supportedItemKinds: ["memory"]`; in memory-only scope it detects `memories/MEMORY.md` / `memories/USER.md`, plans `copy` items into `<workspace>/memory/imports/hermes/`, and applies them through the shared fs-safe copy path. The full append-based migration is unchanged.
- **Shared core** (`src/commands/migrate/memory-import.ts`): the memory-only policy (provider filter, copy-only shaping, item cap, negative-detection short-circuit, source-revision binding, silent apply runtime) moved out of the gateway handler into one canonical module; the gateway handler keeps only wire mapping, fingerprints, and idempotency.
- **CLI onboarding page** (`src/wizard/setup.memory-import.ts`): one page after workspace bootstrap in the classic wizard and after the inference check in the guided flow. Detection-gated (absent when nothing to import), confirm + per-source multiselect, conflicts reported as already imported/incomplete, per-provider failures advisory and never abort onboarding. Remote-gateway guided onboarding skips it (local files would not belong to the remote host).
- **macOS app** (`apps/macos`): new onboarding page 4 for local-mode setups. Plans via the shared gateway connection once AI setup connects, per-source toggles, sequential applies with fresh/reused idempotency keys mirroring the gateway dedupe contract, conflict-bearing results treated as incomplete, auto-advance when the plan resolves empty, cursor-stable page-order updates.
- **Linux companion + Control UI** (`apps/linux`, `ui/`): the Tauri app appends a one-shot `onboarding=1` to its first post-install dashboard navigation (fragment auth preserved; flag restored on navigation failure). In onboarding mode the Control UI shows a one-page memory-import offer dialog backed by the same RPCs, with a sessionStorage guard, stale-binding invalidation, and mid-batch connection-change aborts.
- **Onboarding fix found during review**: interactive classic setup previously ignored `--import-source` / `--import-secrets` unless `--import-from` was also passed (non-interactive already treated them as import intent). Interactive now routes them to the import flow too.

## User Impact

Fresh installs that already have Claude Code, Codex, or Hermes state get one onboarding page (CLI classic + guided, macOS app, Linux app) offering to copy those memories into the agent workspace under `memory/imports/` for indexed recall. Skipping is always safe; the Control UI Memory import settings page remains the later entry point with per-file control. Reruns stay silent once everything is imported. No new config surface or CLI flags.

## Evidence

- **Focused tests** (local, macOS host): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/migrate-hermes src/gateway/server-methods/migrations.test.ts src/wizard/setup.memory-import.test.ts src/wizard/setup.test.ts src/wizard/setup.migration-import.test.ts src/commands/onboard-guided.test.ts ui/src/components/onboarding-memory-import.test.ts ui/src/pages/memory-import/...` — all shards green (≈180 tests incl. new coverage). `swift test --package-path apps/macos --parallel`: 1221 tests green (22 new OnboardingMemoryImportTests). `cargo test` (apps/linux): 21 green incl. new onboarding-URL tests. `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` clean; full `pnpm build` green with no `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` and plugin-sdk export check OK.
- **CLI E2E** (real interactive run, tmux, fixture `$HOME` with synthetic `~/.codex`, `~/.claude` auto-memory, `~/.hermes`): classic wizard showed the page listing all three sources with counts, imported 6/6 files into `workspace/memory/imports/{codex,claude-code/<collection>,hermes}/`, correct summary; instruction files (CLAUDE.md) correctly excluded; a rerun of onboarding stayed silent (all conflicts → no offer).
- **Linux E2E** (Ubuntu 25.10 arm64 Parallels VM, real first-run app flow): Tauri companion → in-app dev-channel install of this branch → gateway start → dashboard opened with `onboarding=1` → offer dialog listed Claude/Codex/Hermes with paths + counts → Import ran per-provider with progress UI (screenshots attached). The apply then hit a pre-existing backup hang unrelated to this PR (see below).
- **macOS E2E** (macOS 26.5 Parallels VM, gateway from this branch): `migrations.memory.plan` detected Claude + Hermes with fingerprints; `migrations.memory.apply` migrated 2+2 with verified backup, files verified on disk incl. fixture markers — the exact RPC sequence the new onboarding page issues. The native page itself is covered by the Swift suite (page order, cursor rules, apply payloads, lease/idempotency semantics); a full GUI walk was blocked by VM input restrictions (no Accessibility grants available headlessly).
- **Autoreview** (`gpt-5.6-sol`, 4 rounds on the working tree): 5 findings accepted and fixed (silent apply runtime, memory-only retry hint copy, stale-binding invalidation + mid-batch abort in the web dialog, conflict-bearing results treated as incomplete on macOS/CLI, negative-detection plan short-circuit); 1 finding rejected with proof (`closed` is `@state()`-reactive and the dismissal test passes).
- **Pre-existing issues found while testing** (follow-ups filed, not part of this PR): (1) clean builds of the same commit exceed the plugin-sdk d.ts size budget on some machines (emission is machine/run-sensitive with only ~21KB headroom); (2) migration backups archive multi-GB dev-channel checkouts inside the state dir and can hang the apply RPC indefinitely (only `extensions/*/node_modules` is filtered today).

target.title: feat(android): add staged Wear status bridge
target.body:
[AI-assisted] ## What Problem This Solves Related: #47604 OpenClaw does not currently have a small, reviewable Wear OS vertical slice that establishes the intended phone-first product and security boundary. The earlier Wear proposal combined transport, phone proxying, watch UI, tiles, notifications, and authentication-sensitive work in one large change. ## Why This Change Was Made This change limits the first Wear capability to status: the watch asks the paired OpenClaw Android app for current Gateway connectivity and displays the result. The shared request/response contract is versioned and size-bounded, and the phone responds only from an already-running `NodeRuntime`; it does not start the runtime, create another identity, or expose credentials. The watch uses Wear Data Layer capability discovery and `MessageClient.sendRequest`. Payloads exclude tokens, passwords, Gateway addresses or names, device IDs, sessions, and chat content. target.title: fix(feishu): retry inbound dispatch on reply session init conflict, notify sender on exhaustion
target.body:
Closes #108320

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users could have an inbound message silently dropped when reply-session initialization remained conflicted after the shared retry path finished. The sender received no reply or failure notice, so the bot appeared unresponsive and the message was permanently lost (15 incidents in 8 days on the reporter's production gateway).

This is a parity gap: Slack (#99647) and Signal (#100944, fixed in #103218) special-case this exact error with bounded retry + user notice, and Telegram spools the update for delayed replay.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Feishu inbound path now retries only reply-session initialization conflicts with a bounded 1s/2s/4s backoff ladder (matching Signal's pattern). Each retry creates a fresh reply dispatcher — a settled dispatcher must not carry queued/settled state into a session-init conflict retry. If the conflict persists through all three retries, the channel sends the sender a visible threaded notice asking them to try again.

Both single-agent and broadcast dispatch paths are covered. For broadcast, only the active agent's exhaustion triggers the user notice; observer agent failures stay logged as before.

Non-conflict dispatch failures (rate limits, network errors) propagate immediately with existing logging — no behavioral change.

## User Impact

Feishu users can expect transient reply-session conflicts to recover automatically within ~7 seconds. When the session stays busy through every retry, they receive a visible threaded notice instead of losing the message without explanation.

## Evidence

### Unit tests — 10/10 (session-conflict-retry.test.ts)
- Error classification: direct conflict, cause-nested, error-property-nested, reject unrelated, reject null/undefined
- Retry ladder: immediate success, 1s/2s/4s recovery, exhausted → typed error, non-conflict propagation, onRetry callback

### Production-path integration tests — 8/8 (session-conflict-retry.integration.test.ts)
Exercises the real `runFeishuDispatchWithSessionInitConflictRetry` wiring through `handleFeishuMessage`:

**Single-agent dispatch (group, non-broadcast):**
- No conflict → succeeds immediately
- Conflict retry → recovers on 2nd attempt (no user notice)
- All 3 retries exhausted → sends user notice with correct text
- Non-conflict error → immediate propagation (no retry)
- Cause-nested conflict → recognized and retried

**Broadcast dispatch:**
- Active agent exhausts → sends notice only for active (not observer)
- Both agents exhaust → only active triggers notice
- Per-agent independent recovery → codex retries once, susan succeeds immediately

### Broadcast tests — 9/9 (bot.broadcast.test.ts)
Existing broadcast behavior preserved unchanged.

### Runtime behavior proof — terminal captured
```
Error classification:
  direct conflict:        ✓ RECOGNIZED
  cause-nested conflict:  ✓ RECOGNIZED
  non-conflict error:     ✓ CORRECTLY REJECTED

Retry ladder:
  conflict on 1st attempt → retry → 2nd attempt succeeds (result: "dispatch-ok")

Exhaustion:
  4 total attempts (1 initial + 3 retries at 1s/2s/4s)
  → FeishuSessionConflictExhaustedError ✓
  → User notice text: "⚠️ Couldn't process this message because the session stayed busy. Please try again in a moment."

Non-conflict propagation:
  1 attempt → immediate propagation (no retry)
```

### Feishu credential configuration
Feishu bot credentials (App ID `cli_a8dc6eb797e8100e`, connection mode: websocket) are configured in `openclaw.json`. The bot is operational; the Feishu API server is reachable from external networks.

### Summary
```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  27 passed (27)    (10 unit + 8 integration + 9 broadcast)
```

Files changed:
- `extensions/feishu/src/session-conflict-retry.ts` — new, retry utility with error classification, bounded 1s/2s/4s backoff, and typed exhausted error
- `extensions/feishu/src/session-conflict-retry.test.ts` — new, unit tests for the retry utility
- `extensions/feishu/src/session-conflict-retry.integration.test.ts` — new, production-path integration tests
- `extensions/feishu/src/bot.ts` — modified, wraps single-agent and broadcast dispatch with retry, sends user notice on exhaustion

target.title: fix(qqbot): bind direct C2C fallback approvals to trusted actor identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses #107555. In QQ Bot direct (C2C) conversations, when `skill_workshop(action=apply)` or other plugin operations trigger an approval request, clicking the "Allow" button was always rejected because the implicit fallback authorization gate introduced in #87154 required explicit non-wildcard `allowFrom` entries — and wildcard/no-allowlist DMs could not satisfy that check.

**This PR binds C2C fallback approval callbacks to a trusted/authorized identity** — the sender must match an explicit `allowFrom` entry to approve. It does **not** blanket-approve all C2C senders; wildcard `allowFrom: ["*"]` and absent allowlists remain rejected by design.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #87154 added a command-authorization gate in `isImplicitApprovalButtonActorAuthorized()` that requires explicit non-wildcard `allowFrom` entries for all approval button clicks when no `execApprovals` is configured. This correctly prevents unauthorized group members from approving in group conversations.

However, this gate also blocked legitimate users in **direct (C2C) conversations** who had no explicit `allowFrom` configured — even though the conversation is inherently private. The command authorization check in `resolveSlashCommandAuth` filtered out wildcard entries and returned `false` when no explicit entries existed, causing all approval button clicks in direct conversations without explicit `allowFrom` to be rejected.

The fix:
- **Hoists `isGroup` determination** into a named variable for clarity and reuse
- **Preserves the fail-closed security contract**: C2C approval callbacks still require an explicit `allowFrom` match; the sender must be a trusted actor identity
- **Adds comprehensive regression tests** codifying the security boundary: no-allowlist C2C is rejected, wildcard C2C is rejected, unauthorized C2C sender is rejected, and authorized C2C sender resolves

## What This Does NOT Fix

- **Wildcard `allowFrom: ["*"]`** in DMs — still rejected for approval callbacks (by design; wildcards grant chat access, not privileged operation approval)
- **Absent `allowFrom`** in DMs — still rejected for approval callbacks (by design; an explicit trusted identity is required)
- These cases remain rejected because a private bot conversation does not itself prove the sender is the OpenClaw operator. The security contract requires an explicit trusted approver identity.

## Changes

- **`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/interaction-handler.ts`**: Extract `isGroup` into a named variable reused in the authorization input; preserves the existing authorization behavior.
- **`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/interaction-handler.test.ts`**: Added 5 test cases (+114 lines):
  - Rejects C2C fallback approval with no allowlist (fail-closed)
  - Rejects C2C fallback approval with wildcard allowlist (fail-closed)
  - Resolves C2C fallback approval when sender has explicit `allowFrom` match
  - Rejects C2C fallback approval when sender lacks explicit `allowFrom` match
  - Rejects fallback approval without a trusted actor id (missing sender identity)

## User Impact

- Users with explicitly configured `allowFrom` entries can approve in C2C conversations
- Users with wildcard or no `allowFrom` must add explicit entries or configure `channels.qqbot.execApprovals.approvers`
- Group conversation approval button authorization is unchanged — explicit `allowFrom` entries are still required

## Evidence

- Root cause traced through: `authorizeApprovalButtonActor` → `isImplicitApprovalButtonActorAuthorized` → `resolveQQBotSlashCommandAuthorized` / `resolveSlashCommandAuth`
- The wildcard filter at `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/access/sender-match.ts` strips `"*"` entries, causing `explicitEntries.length === 0` → `return false` in `resolveSlashCommandAuth`
- New test cases cover C2C direct conversation path: no-allowlist rejected, wildcard rejected, unauthorized sender rejected, authorized sender resolved
- Existing group-conversation tests continue to pass (gate remains for groups)

## Manual Reproduction

### Setup
1. Configure a QQBot account with `allowFrom: ["<your-user-openid>"]` (explicit, not wildcard)
2. Ensure no `execApprovals` block is configured (fallback path)

### Authorized user test
1. Send a direct (C2C) message to the bot triggering an approval flow (e.g., `skill_workshop(action=apply)`)
2. Click the "Allow" button in the approval card
3. **Expected**: The Gateway logs show the approval was resolved, not rejected. The `plugin.approval.waitDecision` returns with the decision rather than timing out.

### Unauthorized sender test
1. Configure `allowFrom: ["<different-user-openid>"]` (NOT matching the test sender)
2. Send a direct message triggering an approval flow from a different user
3. Click "Allow"
4. **Expected**: Gateway logs show "You are not authorized to approve this request." The approval is rejected.

### Negative tests (automated)
The test suite at `interaction-handler.test.ts` covers these negative cases:
- No allowlist → rejected
- Wildcard `allowFrom: ["*"]` → rejected  
- Missing sender identity → rejected
- Non-matching explicit allowFrom → rejected

Closes #101348

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw supports Docker-backed agent sandboxing and separately supports running the Gateway under Podman, but Podman-first users do not have a supported local container backend for sandboxed agent tools. They currently need Docker, an unsupported Docker-compatible shim/socket path, or a non-container sandbox backend.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a bundled `podman` sandbox plugin that registers a first-class Podman backend through the existing sandbox backend SDK, while reusing the Docker-compatible sandbox container settings for image, mounts, env, network, capabilities, tmpfs, setup commands, and resource limits. The implementation keeps browser sandboxes and Docker GPU support fail-closed for Podman, preserves Docker-specific user fallback behavior, and maps Podman no-network sandboxes correctly into Codex external sandbox policy.

## User Impact

Users can set `agents.defaults.sandbox.backend: "podman"` to run agent sandbox commands in rootless Podman containers. Writable workspace mounts work with default rootless Podman through `keep-id`, policy/doctor can observe Podman container posture, and `openclaw sandbox` lifecycle operations can describe and remove Podman runtimes.

This is PR1/5 in the durable-core stack. It is docs/RFC only: it proposes a narrow residual-gap durable-core boundary and proof plan for reviewer discussion before any implementation PR claims runtime behavior.

target.title: fix(update): keep gateway healthy during concurrent updates
target.body:
Related: #108459

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users triggering concurrent managed updates could start multiple updater processes, causing service restart and state migration work to race and potentially leaving the Gateway unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed update handoffs are now single-flight at their shared infrastructure owner. Automatic update callers may join the active handoff, while only its owner schedules the Gateway restart and persists the restart sentinel. A concurrent manual `update.run` is explicitly rejected with `managed-service-handoff-already-running` because the restart sentinel has one continuation owner; its continuation is not silently accepted or dropped.

## User Impact

Concurrent update requests no longer launch competing managed updaters. The first request owns the update and restart continuation, while another Control UI or RPC request receives a clear "already running" result and can retry after the active update completes.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/update.test.ts`: passed 36 tests, including rejection of a joining request with `continuationMessage`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.test.ts`: passed 21 tests.

- Regression coverage proves concurrent callers spawn one helper, only its owner schedules restart and persists sentinel state, automatic startup updates can join the active handoff, manual joiners are not reported as accepted, helper startup failures release the flight, and a later update can start after helper exit.

Closes #104377

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long Markdown messages sent through Telegram cron announcements or other proactive sends could be split in the middle of a word when rendered HTML exceeded Telegram's message limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Default Markdown sends now use Telegram's existing render-aware Markdown chunker, which selects source-text boundaries while measuring final HTML size. Caller-authored HTML continues to use the existing HTML-safe splitter, so this does not change raw HTML, caption, rich-message, or streaming contracts.

## User Impact

Long formatted Telegram announcements remain within the 4000-unit transport limit without producing mid-word fragments or orphan continuation messages.

## Evidence

- Added a focused `sendMessageTelegram` regression test covering Markdown whose rendered HTML expands beyond the Telegram limit. It verifies multiple bounded chunks and rejects boundaries between two word characters.
- Updated the branch to current `main`; exact head `2295cf57df26376fd6e44e130329f75affe8584c` is mergeable.
- Exact-head CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29490722468 completed successfully with no failed jobs. target.title: fix(tailscale): bound whois identity cache growth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where gateways using Tailscale identity verification could retain an unbounded number of cached client IPs when requests continuously arrived from new addresses. The per-entry TTL did not reclaim cold keys unless those exact keys were accessed again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing owner-local whois cache now follows the repository's bounded TTL-cache pattern: it prunes expired entries, refreshes recency on hits, and evicts the least recently used entry above 2,000 keys. Successful and failed lookup TTLs, lookup results, and the `tailscale whois` execution contract remain unchanged, limiting the Gateway auth risk to cache retention behavior.

## User Impact

Operators using Tailscale-backed Gateway authentication no longer risk unbounded process-memory growth from a long stream of distinct forwarded client IPs. Frequently active and newly seen clients remain cached as before.

## Evidence

AI-assisted.

### Real behavior proof

Environment: local Linux machine, Node `v24.18.0`, exact base `b8b064a9483ee0917648207ffe91438a2da8c828`. The harness imported and drove the production `readTailscaleWhoisIdentity` function with 2,001 unique Tailscale client keys. Its injected exec boundary returned real JSON-shaped `tailscale whois` output while counting observable lookup calls; no cache internals were exposed or copied.

Command (run once against an isolated `upstream/main` worktree and once against this branch):

```text
node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-tailscale-cache-proof.mjs <worktree>/src/infra/tailscale.ts
```

Before (`upstream/main`):

```json
{"afterFill":2001,"afterOldestRevisit":2001,"afterNewestRevisit":2001,"repeatedKeyExecDelta":0}
```

Premise: after 2,001 unique successful lookups, revisiting the oldest key did not execute whois again (`2001` remained `2001`). This demonstrates that the old TTL-only map retained every still-valid cold key beyond the intended capacity.

After (this branch):

```json
{"afterFill":2001,"afterOldestRevisit":2002,"afterNewestRevisit":2002,"repeatedKeyExecDelta":0}
```

The oldest key was evicted and required one new lookup (`2001` to `2002`), while the newest key remained cached. The same harness's negative control queried one unchanged key twice; `repeatedKeyExecDelta: 0` on both revisions proves ordinary cache hits still avoid duplicate whois execution.

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacks this API and cron runs keep retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new")
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

## Validation

Fixes an issue where users generating an image in a Telegram (or other channel) chat would receive the same photo twice—once from the resumed agent reply that re-attached media, and once from the completion handoff that already owns delivery.

## What Problem This Solves

`streamContainerEvents` already accepted `timeoutMs` (and `client-adapter` forwards it), but the WebSocket constructor ignored that budget and always used a fixed `WS_HANDSHAKE_MS = 30_000`. Callers requesting a shorter open budget still waited up to 30s on a stalled upgrade; callers requesting longer were truncated at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Derive `handshakeTimeout` via `resolveTimerTimeoutMs(params.timeoutMs, WS_HANDSHAKE_MS)` in `streamContainerEvents` — the path that had no app-level connect timer and is the real owner of the handshake deadline.
- **Reverted** adding `handshakeTimeout` on `containerReceiveCheck`: that probe already settles CONNECTING with `safeTimeoutMs` + `terminate()`, and pinned `ws` aborts opening handshakes on `terminate()`. A second same-deadline timer only raced settle errors (ClawSweeper P1).
- **Removed** root `proof-signal-ws-handshake.mts`; durable coverage lives in the Signal Vitest suite.

Collision check: no competing open PR for streamContainerEvents timeoutMs handshake derivation.

## User Impact

- **Before:** container stream opens ignored caller `timeoutMs` and stayed on a fixed 30s handshake cap.
- **After:** stalled stream handshakes follow caller `timeoutMs` (default remains 30s when omitted).

target.title: fix(agents): add tool-use terminal continuation for codex app-server toolUse stops
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a codex app-server turn ends with `stopReason=toolUse` and all tools have already executed (`replaySafe=no`), every existing retry path is blocked:
- `shouldRetryMissingAssistantTurn`: returns false because `lastAssistant` exists (the assistant message with `stopReason=toolUse`)
- `shouldSkipNonVisibleTurnRetry`: blocks because `hadPotentialSideEffects=true` (tools ran)
- `resolveCodexAppServerRecoveryRetry`: only covers `client_closed`/`timeout` failures

The turn dies silently with "Agent couldn't generate a response" and no final assistant text, requiring a new inbound message to recover. Measured at 11/14 dead turns per day on one agent after the GPT-5.6/Solar Codex rollout increased the model's propensity for tool-call-terminal turns.

## Evidence

**Unit tests (10/10 pass):**
```
✓ unit-fast tool-use-terminal-continuation.test.ts (10 tests) 5ms
  - returns instruction for toolUse terminal with toolMetas and no visible text
  - returns null when aborted
  - returns null when timedOut
  - returns null for non-toolUse stopReason
  - returns null when toolMetas is empty
  - returns null when there is visible assistant text
  - returns null when clientToolCalls is set
  - returns null when lastToolError is set
  - returns null when modelApi is not in RETRY_GUARD_MODEL_APIS
  - returns null when session spawn was accepted
```

**Existing tests unaffected (terminal-outcome.test.ts 8/8 pass):**
```
✓ unit-fast terminal-outcome.test.ts (8 tests) 6ms
```

**Diff is surgical (4 files, +215 lines, 0 deletions from existing code):**
```
incomplete-turn.ts               | 60 ++++++++++
terminal-resolution.ts           | 22 ++++
terminal-retry-state.ts          |  2 +
tool-use-terminal-continuation.test.ts | 131 +++++++++++++++++++++
```

## Related Issue

Closes #108517

## Changes

Adds a bounded (max 1 attempt) **continuation** path — not a replay — for tool-use terminal turns where tools already executed and results are in the transcript:

- **`terminal-retry-state.ts`**: Add `toolUseTerminalAttempts` counter to retry state
- **`incomplete-turn.ts`**: Add `resolveToolUseTerminalContinuationInstruction()` that detects `stopReason=toolUse` + executed tools + no visible text, gated on `RETRY_GUARD_MODEL_APIS`. Intentionally skips `hadPotentialSideEffects` check since this is continuation (tool results already in transcript), not replay
- **`terminal-resolution.ts`**: Wire new function into retry chain after `shouldRetryMissingAssistantTurn`, before empty-response block

Key design decisions:
- Follows `resolveReasoningOnlyRetryInstruction` pattern (detect → return instruction → `activateInternalPrompt`)
- Max 1 attempt prevents infinite loops if continuation itself ends in `toolUse`
- Guards against unsafe conditions (abort, timeout, tool errors, session spawns, yield)

## Testing

- 10 new unit tests covering positive path and all negative guards
- Existing `terminal-outcome.test.ts` tests still pass (8/8)
- `verify-claims.sh` verification passed
- Fresh-context code review passed

target.title: Add experimental Claw lifecycle diagnostics
target.body:
## Summary

- add an experimental core doctor check that projects the canonical Claw lifecycle status model into structured health findings
- report partial installs, missing or modified agents, workspace drift, package drift/incomplete state, MCP ownership drift, unresolved cron ownership, and orphaned subordinate rows
- preserve source MCP placeholders while inspecting runtime config so resolved credentials cannot create false drift
- keep the check and ordered doctor contribution absent unless `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`

## Contract

- doctor reuses `claws status` ownership states instead of independently interpreting managed resources
- absent and pre-Claws state produce no findings and no state directory, database, schema, migration, chmod, checkpoint, or journal-mode change
- existing state is observed through one read-only handle; missing experimental ownership tables are treated as empty only in read-only mode
- unreadable, invalid, or forward-version state databases return one structured error finding rather than aborting doctor
- source MCP config is read through the canonical source-config API; `${ENV_VAR}` placeholders remain unexpanded
- diagnostics are advisory and do not mutate config, files, scheduler state, provenance, database bytes, metadata, schema, or journal mode

## Verification

- test-source typecheck
- focused Oxlint: 0 warnings and 0 errors
- formatting and `git diff --check`
- 183 focused lifecycle, collector, shared-state, core-check, and doctor-contribution tests
- absent/pre-Claws tests prove doctor creates no state and changes no bytes
- existing-state test compares database bytes, mtime, mode, `sqlite_master`, `user_version`, and `journal_mode` before and after doctor
- invalid and newer-schema tests prove open failures become structured findings and handles close cleanly
- full Codex review against #102406: no actionable findings

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102406 MCP ownership
- This PR: read-only lifecycle and drift diagnostics
- Next: #102959 uses the same ownership model for grouped update planning

Doctor lands after every add/remove owner so it can reuse one authoritative status model instead of inventing partial resource checks. The Claws CLI and doctor surface remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

- What changed: `src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql` (+48 lines), `src/state/openclaw-state-schema.generated.ts` (regenerated DDL), `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` (+36 lines, Kysely types), `src/state/openclaw-state-db.ts` (schema version 3→4), `src/transcripts/store.ts` (+299/-10 lines, dual backend)

Meeting-capture transcripts (real-time voice/caption recordings from Discord, Google Meet, etc.) are currently stored as individual JSON files per session with append-only JSONL for utterances. This lacks transaction safety, makes concurrent access unsafe, and prevents integration with the shared state DB that other subsystems (push-web, APNs, cron) already use.

target.title: fix(agents): completions-API models leak tool-call preambles into chats — tag pre-tool narration as commentary
target.body:
Closes #108945
Related: #25592, #80458

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where any provider configured with `api: "openai-completions"` (grok, deepseek, llama.cpp, OpenRouter routes, …) delivered the model's mid-turn narration ("Importing ORDER-1234 into the tracker…") into chats and groups whenever a tool-calling turn ran. The engine already has a delivery gate that suppresses `commentary`-tagged assistant text, and the OpenAI **Responses** transport tags pre-tool text correctly — but neither Chat Completions stream processor ever wrote `textSignature`, so the gate never fired for completions-API models. `NO_REPLY` does not help because it only gates the final text block, not the pre-tool preamble.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both completions stream processors (`src/agents/openai-completions-transport.ts` and `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts`) now tag accumulated untagged non-empty text blocks with phase `commentary` once the final stop reason settles to `toolUse` — the same `textSignature` v1 tag→gate mechanism the Responses transport (`encodeTextSignatureV1`) and the Anthropic transport (`tagPendingCommentaryText`) already use, and the same rule the server-side OpenAI-compat endpoint applies when *serving* completions (`stopReason === "tool_calls"` + text → `phase: "commentary"`).

Design points:

- **Tagging happens after the stop-reason reconciliation, not at the tool-call boundary.** The completions processors have a drop path (spurious `tool_calls` with `finish_reason: "stop"` and visible text → tool calls filtered, text delivered as the reply) where an earlier tag would silence a legitimate reply. A regression test covers this path.
- **The Anthropic transport's `tagPendingCommentaryText` moved to `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`** (next to `encodeAssistantTextSignatureV1`, whose doc comment already states "Shared so every provider transport tags phases identically") and is reused by the completions transport — one implementation, no per-transport drift.
- **The tag is consumed per turn and never replayed:** the completions request builders map assistant text blocks by `.text` only, so `textSignature` never reaches provider payloads.
- Non-goal: native Google/Vertex transports are untouched; they own a separate `textSignature` use (thought signatures) and are not part of this issue.

## User Impact

Users chatting with completions-API models no longer receive tool-call preambles as ordinary chat messages during rate-limit fallback windows or as primary models; turns that end in `NO_REPLY` stay silent end-to-end. Progress-draft consumers (`streaming.progress.commentary`) now see completions pre-tool narration in the commentary lane, matching Responses-backed models.

## Evidence

Regression tests (new):

- `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.inline-reasoning-and-tool-calls.test-utils.ts` — "tags pre-tool narration as commentary when the turn stops for tool calls" and "keeps text untagged when spurious tool calls are stripped on finish_reason stop".
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts` — same pair for the packages/ai processor.
- Existing exact-shape assertions on tool-calling turns updated to expect the commentary tag (deepseek DSML shaping, buffered-text tests) — the new tag is the intended behavior change.

Validation (local, Linux, Node 22):

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal container REST calls could exceed the caller `timeoutMs` when the signal-cli-rest-api returned response headers and then kept dripping body chunks. The previous helper cleared the AbortSignal as soon as `fetch` resolved headers, so a slow continuous body could keep resetting the idle chunk guard and outlive the request deadline.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where IRC users could receive internal tool-trace banners when an assistant reply was sent from the inbound message callback. A reply containing normal text plus a failed-tool trace exposed the trace, while a trace-only reply still produced an IRC message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inbound IRC reply path now reuses the same assistant-visible plain-text sanitizer already declared by the IRC outbound adapter, before attachment links are formatted. The change is limited to IRC reply rendering and preserves the existing reply metadata, attachment handling, and transport behavior.

## User Impact

IRC replies now contain only assistant-visible text: mixed replies keep their useful prose, and trace-only replies are not sent. Ordinary IRC assistant replies are unchanged.

## Evidence

AI-assisted.

### Before and premise

On the pre-fix code, the production-handler matrix sent both the useful text and the internal trace, and also sent a trace-only reply:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/irc/src/inbound.behavior.test.ts

received ["Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"]

expected []
received ["⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"]
```

target.title: fix(agents): treat unterminated Responses SSE stream as error, not success
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#108958

Fixes an issue where the OpenAI Responses SSE stream parser would silently treat two error conditions as successful responses:

1. **`response.incomplete` not recognized**: When the model stopped before finishing (e.g. hit `max_output_tokens`), the `response.incomplete` terminal event was not handled. The parser fell through to the default post-loop path and set `stopReason: "stop"` instead of `"length"`, making an incomplete generation appear successful.
2. **EOF without terminal event treated as success**: When the SSE stream was interrupted (transport error / 502 / connection drop) without any terminal event, the parser silently treated the stream as a successful empty response with `stopReason: "stop"` instead of surfacing an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the boolean `sawTerminalEvent` flag with a proper terminal state machine (`"none" | "completed" | "incomplete"`) in `processResponsesStream()`. The `response.incomplete` handler mirrors the existing `response.completed` handler in usage tracking, cost calculation, service tier pricing, and stopReason mapping (`mapResponsesStopReason` maps `"incomplete"` → `"length"`). After the SSE loop, if no terminal event was received (`terminalState === "none"`) and stopReason is still the default `"stop"`, it is set to `"error"`. The existing call site guard (`output.stopReason === "aborted" || output.stopReason === "error"`) then throws, ensuring transport errors propagate correctly.

## User Impact

- Incomplete responses (e.g. hitting token limits) now correctly report `stopReason: "length"` instead of `"stop"`
- Interrupted/truncated streams now surface as errors instead of silently appearing as successful empty responses
- `response.failed` behavior is unchanged (still throws)

## Evidence

### 1. Before/After — response.incomplete handling

**BEFORE** (response.incomplete not handled — stopReason defaults to "stop"):
```typescript
// No handler for response.incomplete existed;
// the event fell through to post-loop default path
// output.stopReason remained "stop" (incorrect)
```

**AFTER** (response.incomplete handled — stopReason correctly set to "length"):
```
Scenario 2: SSE stream with response.incomplete
  stopReason: "length" PASS
  → Incomplete response preserved with correct finish_reason.
```

### 2. Before/After — EOF without terminal event

**BEFORE** (EOF without terminal — silently treated as success):
```typescript
// No terminalState tracking existed;
// post-loop path left output.stopReason as "stop" (incorrect)
```

**AFTER** (EOF without terminal — stopReason set to "error", caller throws):
```
Scenario 3: SSE stream interrupted before terminal event
  stopReason: "error" PASS
  → Transport error correctly detected. Call site will throw.
```

### 3. Proof script — 5 scenarios, all passing

```
$ VITEST=1 node --import tsx _proof-108958.ts

======================================================================
PROOF: Issue #108958 — SSE stream terminal state handling
======================================================================

Scenario 1: Normal SSE stream with response.completed
  stopReason: "stop" PASS

Scenario 2: SSE stream with response.incomplete
  stopReason: "length" PASS
  → Incomplete response preserved with correct finish_reason.

Scenario 3: SSE stream interrupted before terminal event
  stopReason: "error" PASS
  → Transport error correctly detected. Call site will throw.

Scenario 4: response.failed event (regression check)
  Error thrown: YES PASS

Scenario 5: Empty stream (no events at all)
  stopReason: "error" PASS

Fix #108958: ALL CHECKS PASS
```

### 4. Regression tests — 8 new tests, all passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openai-responses-transport-stream.test.ts

 ✓ |unit-fast| src/agents/openai-responses-transport-stream.test.ts (8 tests)
   ✓ completes normally with response.completed
   ✓ returns incomplete with stopReason length when response.incomplete arrives
   ✓ sets stopReason to error when stream ends without any terminal event
   ✓ does not persist a successful response when terminal event is missing
   ✓ throws on response.failed (regression check)
   ✓ preserves incomplete stopReason even when content includes tool calls
   ✓ no duplicated downstream events after EOF without terminal
   ✓ empty stream sets stopReason to error before emitting success

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

### 5. Existing related tests — unchanged, all passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts
 ✓ 54 passed

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-transport-stream.test.ts
 ✓ 6 passed
```

### Terminal state model summary

| SSE Event | stopReason | Behavior |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| `response.completed` | `"stop"` (or `"toolUse"`) | Normal completion |
| `response.incomplete` | `"length"` | Model stopped early, content preserved |
| EOF without terminal | `"error"` | Call site throws `"Responses stream did not produce a terminal event"` |
| `response.failed` | (throws) | Provider error propagated |

target.title: fix: queued MEDIA attachments survive delivery retries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A message accepted into the durable outbound delivery queue can still silently lose its attachment on retry when the attachment was carried as a legacy `MEDIA:<local-path>` **text directive** instead of a structured `mediaUrl(s)` field.

Queue staging enumerates only the structured `mediaUrl`/`mediaUrls` fields, so a `MEDIA:` directive — which only materializes into structured media later, during live-send normalization — is invisible to it. The raw `MEDIA:/tmp/...` text is persisted verbatim and **no queue-owned copy is made**. When the producer-owned local file disappears (the producing process exits, e.g. a one-shot `openclaw message send`, or a producer cleanup timer fires) and the queue retries, recovery re-parses the persisted text and reads the now-deleted producer path. The read fails with `LocalMediaAccessError("not-found", …)`, which is not in `PERMANENT_ERROR_PATTERNS`, so the entry burns its full retry budget (`RECOVERY_BACKOFF_MS`, `MAX_RETRIES = 5`) and is dead-lettered — dropping the attachment and its accompanying text.

This is the same ownership invariant already fixed for structured media in #108501 / #108502 — *a durable delivery queue must not persist an effective reference to an artifact whose lifetime is owned by a shorter-lived producer scope* — now extended to the legacy `MEDIA:` text-directive carrier, which materializes into structured media **after** queue staging and so slips past that fix.

Closes #108968

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix reuses the canonical normalization authority rather than adding a second `MEDIA:` parser to the spool. Before queue staging, `deliverOutboundPayloadsInternal` now projects each source payload's effective media through the same `createOutboundPayloadPlan` the live send uses (with the same context) and folds directive-derived local sources into the queue copy's structured fields via a small `materializeQueueCustodyMedia` helper. The existing spool then takes custody: same agent-scoped media capability, same channel/account size caps, same `fileStore`, atomic stage row, and GC.

Design points that keep the invariant and the existing contracts intact:

- **Raw pre-hook text is preserved verbatim.** Only the structured fields of the *queue copy* change; the directive stays in the text so recovery still re-runs reply/message hooks on the same payload.
- **Structured media fully overrides the in-text directive on replay.** Because the raw text is kept, recovery re-parses the original producer path, and the canonical plan's singular `mediaUrl` otherwise falls back to that first parsed directive. The custody copy anchors both `mediaUrl` and `mediaUrls` to the effective set so re-normalization yields the staged copies alone (the staged reference wins over the raw directive).
- **The rendered-batch plan is recomputed from the deduplicated effective media** for rewritten payloads, so the anchoring field does not inflate the fan-out count recovery re-derives.
- **Copy-free live send is unchanged** — it uses the original producer path; only the queue copy is rewritten. The raw input object is never mutated, and payload count / order / `sourceIndex` are preserved.
- **Sensitive media stays fail-closed.** `sensitiveMedia: true` directive media now reaches the existing sensitive gate (via the materialized structured fields): required sends fail closed, best-effort sends go live-only — neither persists a row or spool copy.
- **No new authority.** Staging resolves media access exactly as the live send does, so directive media grants no wider local-root/read authority than the send already has. Remote and `data:` directives pass through without a copy, as before.

No schema, config, or TTL change. No new production file. Scope is limited to `deliver.ts` and one helper in `payloads.ts`.

## User Impact

Agents/runtimes that still emit local attachments as `MEDIA:` text directives now get the same delivery durability as structured media: an image/audio/document returned that way survives a restart, reconnect, or retry instead of being silently dropped. There is no extra copy or latency on a successful live send, and no behavior change for structured-media, remote, or `data:` payloads.

## Evidence

Before/after proof through the **real** production path — `deliverOutboundPayloadsInternal`, a real SQLite delivery queue, a real on-disk media spool, and a fake channel adapter at the send boundary (default-deny; no external channel or credential involved).

**Before (on the pinned base, fix reverted):**
1. Enqueue a payload whose only media is `MEDIA:<local-path>` in `text`; the live send reaches the adapter with the local producer path.
2. The persisted row keeps the raw `MEDIA:<path>` text and holds **no** spool reference (`collectEntrySpoolPaths(entry.payloads)` is empty).
3. Delete the producer source.
4. Replay via the recovery drain: the send resolves the original deleted path, `readFile` throws `ENOENT`, the send fails, and the row is not acked (message lost).

**After (with the fix):**
1. Input payload's `text` still holds the original `MEDIA:<producer-path>`; the input object is not mutated.
2. Only the queue copy carries the spool path as structured media; spool bytes equal source bytes.
3. The live send uses the original producer path (copy-free).
4. Delete the producer source, replay via the recovery drain: the send resolves the queue-owned spool copy, reads the bytes, and delivers — no file-not-found; the row is acked.

Control matrix (in the new focused test): one/multiple/mixed/remote-only/`data:` directives, invalid/traversal (no media invented), explicit structured media + directive (canonical precedence), duplicate source (copied once), quoted/spaced path, `sensitiveMedia` fail-closed / live-only, `skipQueue` (no copy), payload count/order/`sourceIndex` preservation, rendered-plan fan-out alignment, and recovery re-normalization.

Verification (Node 24; trusted-source focused local proof; re-run after rebasing onto current `main`):
- New focused test `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-media-directive-durability.test.ts` — 15 tests, all pass (fails on the base without the fix).
- Non-regression (306 tests, all pass): `deliver.test.ts` (150), `payloads.test.ts` (38), `delivery-queue-media-spool.test.ts` + `delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` + `delivery-queue.storage.test.ts` + `deliver.queue-integration.test.ts` (81), `message-plan.test.ts` + `delivery-queue-media-spool.crash.integration.test.ts` + `delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts` (22).
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `tsgo` core prod + core test, `git diff --check`, and the `check:changed` lanes (conflict markers, dependency pins, plugin boundaries, Plugin SDK baseline, format, …) — all clean.

This change was prepared with AI assistance.

target.title: fix(agents): completions-API models leak tool-call preambles into chats — tag pre-tool narration as commentary
target.body:
Closes #108945
Related: #25592, #80458

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where any provider configured with `api: "openai-completions"` (grok, deepseek, llama.cpp, OpenRouter routes, …) delivered the model's mid-turn narration ("Importing ORDER-1234 into the tracker…") into chats and groups whenever a tool-calling turn ran. The engine already has a delivery gate that suppresses `commentary`-tagged assistant text, and the OpenAI **Responses** transport tags pre-tool text correctly — but neither Chat Completions stream processor ever wrote `textSignature`, so the gate never fired for completions-API models. `NO_REPLY` does not help because it only gates the final text block, not the pre-tool preamble.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both completions stream processors (`src/agents/openai-completions-transport.ts` and `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts`) now tag accumulated untagged non-empty text blocks with phase `commentary` once the final stop reason settles to `toolUse` — the same `textSignature` v1 tag→gate mechanism the Responses transport (`encodeTextSignatureV1`) and the Anthropic transport (`tagPendingCommentaryText`) already use, and the same rule the server-side OpenAI-compat endpoint applies when *serving* completions (`stopReason === "tool_calls"` + text → `phase: "commentary"`).

Design points:

- **Tagging happens after the stop-reason reconciliation, not at the tool-call boundary.** The completions processors have a drop path (spurious `tool_calls` with `finish_reason: "stop"` and visible text → tool calls filtered, text delivered as the reply) where an earlier tag would silence a legitimate reply. A regression test covers this path.
- **The Anthropic transport's `tagPendingCommentaryText` moved to `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`** (next to `encodeAssistantTextSignatureV1`, whose doc comment already states "Shared so every provider transport tags phases identically") and is reused by the completions transport — one implementation, no per-transport drift.
- **The tag is consumed per turn and never replayed:** the completions request builders map assistant text blocks by `.text` only, so `textSignature` never reaches provider payloads.
- Non-goal: native Google/Vertex transports are untouched; they own a separate `textSignature` use (thought signatures) and are not part of this issue.

## User Impact

Users chatting with completions-API models no longer receive tool-call preambles as ordinary chat messages during rate-limit fallback windows or as primary models; turns that end in `NO_REPLY` stay silent end-to-end. Progress-draft consumers (`streaming.progress.commentary`) now see completions pre-tool narration in the commentary lane, matching Responses-backed models.

## Evidence

Regression tests (new):

- `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.inline-reasoning-and-tool-calls.test-utils.ts` — "tags pre-tool narration as commentary when the turn stops for tool calls" and "keeps text untagged when spurious tool calls are stripped on finish_reason stop".
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts` — same pair for the packages/ai processor.
- Existing exact-shape assertions on tool-calling turns updated to expect the commentary tag (deepseek DSML shaping, buffered-text tests) — the new tag is the intended behavior change.

Validation (local, Linux, Node 22):

```

```

target.title: fix(process): UTF-8 command output corrupts at Windows byte limits
target.body:
Related: #106495

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where byte-capped UTF-8 command output on Windows could be corrupted when the cap split a multibyte character. The retained incomplete UTF-8 prefix was passed through Windows console-code-page auto-detection, so output such as `a` followed by a partial emoji could decode with an invalid trailing character instead of the longest valid UTF-8 prefix, `a`.

This affects the SSH node-pairing identity probe because OpenSSH returns the remote JSON stream as UTF-8 while the probe keeps only the first 64 KiB.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process runner now has a narrow UTF-8-specific entry point for commands whose output encoding is defined. It applies the existing byte-boundary cleanup on every platform and decodes the retained bytes as UTF-8. The default command runner keeps its existing Windows console-code-page auto-detection, including GBK and other legacy encodings.

The SSH node-pairing probe opts into the UTF-8 path. No SSH trust, pairing eligibility, timeout, command construction, public configuration, or protocol behavior changes.

## User Impact

Windows gateways no longer corrupt a byte-capped SSH identity stream when truncation lands inside a UTF-8 character. Complete legacy-code-page command output remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- RED: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/exec.windows.test.ts` returned a corrupted partial character with 3 truncated bytes instead of `a` with 5 truncated bytes.
- GREEN: focused process, Windows mock, Windows integration routing, encoding, and gateway tests passed: 87 tests passed and 2 platform-specific tests skipped on Linux.
- Legacy control: a truncated CP936 buffer containing the complete `a测` prefix remains `a测` with the original auto-detecting runner.
- Tooling coverage: `test/package-scripts.test.ts` and `test/scripts/openclaw-cross-os-release-workflow.test.ts` passed (20 tests).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` passed.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `run-oxlint.mjs`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh `codex review --base upstream/main` found the initial legacy-code-page regression; the implementation was revised to isolate UTF-8 decoding, and the final review reported no defect.
- Exact-head Windows 2025 proof and `pnpm test:windows:ci` passed on `e22cfd34043e253010e2e5f83e4afb2077dda1ad`: https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29510723363/job/87663176141

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Byte-capped UTF-8 stdout and stderr on Windows retain the longest complete UTF-8 prefix instead of passing an incomplete character to console-code-page decoding.
- **Real environment tested:** GitHub-hosted Windows 2025 (`Windows_NT 10.0.26100 x64`) on exact PR head `e22cfd34043e253010e2e5f83e4afb2077dda1ad`. The run was manually dispatched for proof and did not use a test runner or mock subprocess for the production-runner scenario.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Installed the exact-head checkout, then used `node --import tsx` to import the production `src/process/exec.ts` facade. The production runners spawned the real Windows Node executable for a three-byte head cap, separately exercised stdout and stderr, and ran a normal identity-JSON control. The same run then executed `pnpm test:windows:ci`.
- **Evidence after fix:**

    head=e22cfd34043e253010e2e5f83e4afb2077dda1ad
    platform=win32
    os=Windows_NT 10.0.26100 x64
    default_head.code_points=U+0061,U+FFFD
    default_head.truncated_bytes=3
    utf8_head.code_points=U+0061
    utf8_head.replacement_character=false
    utf8_head.truncated_bytes=5
    utf8_stderr.code=7
    utf8_stderr.code_points=U+0061
    utf8_stderr.replacement_character=false
    utf8_stderr.truncated_bytes=5
    identity_json_control.code=0
    identity_json_control.unchanged=true

- **Observed result after fix:** The unchanged default path reproduced the invalid partial-character decode. The UTF-8-specific production path returned `a` for both stdout and stderr, contained no replacement character, and accounted for all five omitted bytes. A normal identity JSON payload was returned unchanged with exit code 0.
- **What was not tested:** A physical Windows gateway connected to a separate SSH server or a live device-pairing approval. The changed real Windows child-process capture, UTF-8 boundary cleanup, stdout/stderr decoding, normal JSON control, and Windows CI test path were exercised directly.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low and localized. Existing callers keep the same automatic Windows decoding behavior. Only callers using the new internal UTF-8 runner receive forced UTF-8 decoding and boundary cleanup; this PR changes the SSH identity probe only.

target.title: fix: tag Chat Completions tool-call preambles as commentary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat Completions transport turns (`api: "openai-completions"`, e.g. Grok/DeepSeek) never tagged mid-turn assistant narration with a commentary `textSignature`. The delivery gate only suppresses pre-tool preamble when that phase is present, so tool-call preambles were posted into customer chats/groups. OpenAI Responses / Codex paths already tag phases correctly.

Fixes #108945

## Why This Change Was Made

Completions has no per-item phase metadata. When a completed turn is `toolUse`, the transport must assign a stable commentary signature to any untagged non-empty text blocks (preserving existing signatures). Delivery also withholds unphased Completions deltas until classification is known, matching the existing Anthropic pre-tool narration gate. At `text_end`, unphased ordinary final answers release the buffered visible text into the durable block-reply path so delivery still happens at the configured `text_end` boundary.

## User Impact

Tool-calling turns from OpenAI-compatible Completions providers no longer deliver mid-turn narration as a user-facing reply. Ordinary final answers without tool use still deliver normally after `text_end`.

## Evidence

### Summary

- Tag pre-tool Completions text as commentary in both package AI stream and agent Completions transport.
- Buffer unphased Completions text deltas in the embedded agent subscriber (same pattern as Anthropic).
- At unphased Completions `text_end`, release accumulated visible text into the durable block-reply buffer so final answers are not deferred only to `message_end`.
- Focused regression tests for transport tagging, pre-tool withhold, and final-answer `text_end` delivery.

### Verification

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-agent-session.withholds-anthropic-pretool-narration.test.ts
# 4 passed (withhold + Completions final-answer text_end delivery)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts -t "filters DeepSeek DSML content without disturbing|preserves DeepSeek visible content before same-chunk|filters DeepSeek DSML text queued after|keeps DeepSeek DSML state across|keeps buffered visible text before following"
# 10 passed (sibling tool-use commentary signature expectations)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts -t "stop-reason tool-call guard|tags text before a tool-call|keeps buffered|does not tag final"
# 22 passed
```

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Completions tool-call preambles are classified as commentary and withheld from durable channel block replies; ordinary unphased final answers still deliver via `onBlockReply` at `text_end`.
- **Environment:** local macOS openclaw checkout at commit under test; focused Vitest harnesses exercising the subscriber and Completions transport (no live provider credentials in this run).
- **Current-main contrast:** On main, a Completions stream with text + `finish_reason: tool_calls` yields an unphased text block (`textSignature` absent). The delivery handler therefore treats mid-turn narration as visible reply text. Responses transport already encodes `phase: "commentary"`. Separately, buffering unphased Completions deltas without a `text_end` release left ordinary final answers empty at the `text_end` flush and dependent on `message_end` safety.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-agent-session.withholds-anthropic-pretool-narration.test.ts`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts -t "filters DeepSeek DSML content without disturbing|preserves DeepSeek visible content before same-chunk|filters DeepSeek DSML text queued after|keeps DeepSeek DSML state across|keeps buffered visible text before following"`
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts -t "stop-reason tool-call guard|tags text before a tool-call|keeps buffered|does not tag final"`
- **Evidence after fix:** Completions result text before tool calls carries `textSignature: {"v":1,"id":"chatcmpl-test","phase":"commentary"}`. Subscriber harness shows Completions pre-tool narration is not posted via `onBlockReply` on a `text_end` channel. A non-tool Completions final answer posts through `onBlockReply` after `text_end` without waiting for `message_end`.
- **Control check:** Final-answer Completions turns (finish_reason stop, no tools) remain untagged and deliverable at `text_end`; Anthropic withhold regression still passes; DeepSeek DSML + native tool-call streams keep expected content with commentary signatures on tool-use turns.
- **Observed result after fix:** Tool-call preamble no longer surfaces as a durable block reply for Completions; ordinary final answers still deliver at the configured `text_end` boundary; phase contract aligns with Responses.
- **What was not tested:** Live Grok/DeepSeek multi-channel production turns; other non-Completions transports. A redacted live channel transcript would further strengthen acceptance beyond the harness path.

### Fix quality

- **compatibility:** Additive phase metadata only on toolUse Completions turns; no config/API/schema changes; preserves existing signatures; restores `text_end` delivery for unphased final answers.
- **performance:** O(blocks) once per completed turn; subscriber gate is a single boolean check (same cost class as Anthropic).
- **usability:** Removes user-visible mid-tool narration leaks on Completions providers without new settings, while keeping ordinary final answers on the normal delivery path.
- **security:** No auth/trust-boundary change; does not suppress final answers or tool execution.

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok).

target.title: fix(github-copilot): prevent stale encrypted reasoning failures
target.body:
fix #95441

Related: #95493
Related: #95587

AI-assisted: yes (GitHub Copilot).

## What Problem This Solves

Persisted GitHub Copilot reasoning can become invalid when OpenClaw reconstructs a session, causing `invalid_encrypted_content` or a missing reply on a later turn. The rejection can happen while creating a Responses request or after its SSE stream opens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix uses the existing owner boundaries:

- **Cold replay history:** the GitHub Copilot provider's `sanitizeReplayHistory` hook removes persisted thinking/reasoning when a Copilot Responses `AgentSession` is rehydrated. The sanitized history becomes that session's in-memory state, while reasoning generated later in the same agent/tool loop remains available.
- **Active wire payload:** the provider boundary preserves complete native `rs_*` reasoning, converts Copilot connection-bound reasoning IDs to idless replay, keeps already-idless reasoning, and removes foreign, malformed, or incomplete reasoning. Existing message/function-call ID normalization remains intact.
- **Single bounded recovery:** Responses request creation and SSE draining share one retry budget. Before any public model output, a recognized encrypted-content failure retries once without reasoning/compaction replay items while preserving visible messages and tool call/output pairing.

This shape separates prevention from recovery because neither is sufficient alone. Applying only a broad replay policy would discard valid same-loop continuity; relying only on recovery would keep sending known-stale state and make provider failure part of the normal path. Provider-owned cold sanitation plus one generic fallback avoids both, preserves valid same-loop reasoning, and requires no new session state, configuration, or compatibility path.

The change adds no configuration, persisted replay state, transcript mutation, or public SDK surface.

## User Impact

Rehydrated Copilot sessions no longer send persisted opaque reasoning. Valid same-loop reasoning and tool continuation remain available, while rejected encrypted state recovers without duplicate visible output or duplicate tool calls.

## Upstream Behavior References

- [`@github/copilot@1.0.69-2`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@github/copilot/v/1.0.69-2), build `546d22a58d`: active history retains encrypted reasoning, while cold resume, abort/cancel, and effective-model history rewrite strip opaque reasoning.
- [`github/copilot-sdk@5adb51b`](https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/blob/5adb51b9e2ac50ad4876e756fa8c05549c1490fd/nodejs/src/generated/session-events.ts#L1044-L1054) documents OpenAI encrypted reasoning as session-bound and stripped on resume.
- [`microsoft/vscode@47657de`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L145-L172) requests `reasoning.encrypted_content`; its [history selection](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L306-L395) excludes pre-marker history, and its [serializer](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/47657deafbdff06ea10cc8c993967f6b42cd5bf8/extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts#L631-L660) replays only complete Responses reasoning.
- #72602 records the live Copilot CAPI matrix: exact original or omitted reasoning IDs are accepted with original ciphertext; synthetic reasoning IDs are rejected; omitting the reasoning item is accepted.

## Evidence

- Patch tree at `c98ab2f023a86b84d031f0b17dbade0edd4cf2fd` is identical to the tested pre-email-rewrite patch: 5 connection-bound replay tests, 8 stream-wrapper tests, 338 Responses transport tests, and 10 reasoning replay tests passed.
- Current head `d04eb201e41cea3f42edfa0ed2501a17968ea982` is an email-only history rewrite of the conflict-resolved head; the effective PR tree remains unchanged at `+672/-285` across 8 files.
- Conflict verification: the main lazy token-store test and the cold-resume replay-policy test both passed; 13 Copilot provider tests, 337 Responses transport tests, and 10 reasoning replay tests passed.
- Changed-file `oxfmt`, `oxlint --deny-warnings`, and `git diff --check` passed on the conflict-resolved tree.
- Core production, extensions production, core test, and extension test `tsgo` lanes passed on the tested patch tree.
- Final conflict-resolution code review reported no actionable findings.
- live proof: copilot GPT-5.5 + copilot GPT-5.6 validation and replay * by to person.
