target.title: perf(agents): scope subagent registry reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Supersedes PR #105489 for issue #105423. Controller-scoped subagent reads were hydrating the entire persisted registry. This focused refresh scopes controller and child-session reads to SQLite while preserving current-main persistence, migration, and in-memory precedence behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SQLite store owns indexed scoped predicates. Registry state owns a bounded 500 ms, 64-entry process-local cache, and every successful registry write invalidates its scoped snapshots. Controller reads retain the null-controller requester-only legacy fallback; child reads retain generation ordering.

## User Impact

Large registries no longer require full persisted hydration for controller lists or child latest/display lookups. Existing migration, active/ended in-memory precedence, and broad tree/index APIs remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- CI found one lint violation in the scoped child ordering path; current head `f0594fbc8ff380a5319795286077c4668a11208e` replaces mutating `sort()` with equivalent `toSorted()`.
- Targeted OXLint and `src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts` pass (5/5).
- Focused registry suite on the parent behavior commit: 4 files, 131/131 tests passed in 24.45 seconds.
- Representative SQLite proof seeded 4,080 rows. Baseline and scoped controller results were exactly equivalent (1,056 IDs); child results were exactly equivalent (8 IDs), with lower elapsed time and peak RSS for scoped reads.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`, targeted `oxfmt --check`, per-task review, and final whole-branch review passed before the CI lint follow-up.
- CI core gate, lint, production types, test types, and all selected test shards pass on the current head.

## CI note

The remaining iOS Periphery failures are runner-environment failures while Homebrew installs xcodegen (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/xcodegen/2.46.0 is not a directory`). They are unrelated to this agents/SQLite-only diff; `openclaw/ci-gate` passed.

## Proof gaps

- The prior local changed gate was stopped after its temporary driver caused fail-safe all-lane typechecking; it had no failure output, but it did not complete.
- Fresh automated review could not complete in this environment after two infrastructure failures: the Codex engine's sandboxed Git diff could not spawn its external helper, and the Claude engine is not authenticated.

target.title: fix(anthropic): honor server retry timing
target.body:
Closes #103849

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Anthropic API rate-limit and overload responses lost their HTTP status and `Retry-After` timing before reaching session auto-retry. OpenClaw could retry earlier than the server-requested cooldown, increasing the chance of repeated failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

Anthropic transport errors now carry provider-generic HTTP status and retry timing metadata through the shared assistant-message projection. Session auto-retry treats the provider delay as a lower bound, capped at 60 seconds, while retaining the existing exponential backoff whenever it is longer.

## User Impact

Anthropic sessions respect server-provided cooldown timing for retryable failures instead of retrying prematurely. Providers that do not supply retry metadata keep the existing retry behavior.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `c3831a1a1a87dae78f16c595ff61da93277eafcb`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/transport-stream-shared.test.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts src/agents/sessions/sdk.test.ts`: 143/143 tests passed.
- `git diff origin/main --check`: passed.
- Coverage proves Anthropic `Retry-After` parsing, shared metadata projection, provider-delay lower-bound behavior, the 60-second cap, and preservation of longer exponential backoff.
- The rebased patch has the same stable patch id (`fccbb9fef700cdd70b012724f2c0b44169b98bbf`) as the previously clean Claude autoreview version.
- Blacksmith Testbox was unavailable because the local `blacksmith` CLI is not installed. A fresh exact-head Claude autoreview attempt timed out at the review-engine layer without returning findings; the pre-rebase identical patch had completed clean review.

target.title: fix(voice-call): clamp continue poll RPCs to remaining deadline
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `voicecall continue` polling could overrun the configured continue deadline. The poll loop already clamped sleep to remaining time, but each `voicecall.continue.result` gateway RPC still used a full 5s timeout, so the final iteration could exceed the user-facing timeout by almost one full RPC budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compute `remainingMs` each poll iteration and pass `min(VOICE_CALL_GATEWAY_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, remainingMs)` into `callVoiceCallGateway`. Also stop when remaining sleep is zero so the loop fails closed at the deadline instead of scheduling another full wait.

## User Impact

**Before:** A continue poll near the deadline could wait up to ~5s past the advertised timeout.

**After:** Continue result polls and sleeps stay within the remaining continue deadline.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.ts`, `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts`
- Production caller path: `voicecall continue` → `pollVoiceCallContinueGateway` → `callVoiceCallGateway("voicecall.continue.result", { timeoutMs: remaining })`

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Continue-result gateway RPCs no longer arm a full 5s timeout when less time remains on the poll deadline.

### Canonical reachability path

`registerVoiceCallCli` `continue` action → `pollVoiceCallContinueGateway` → `callGatewayFromCli("voicecall.continue.result", { timeout: String(remainingMs) })`.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted worktree on latest `upstream/main`; focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
✓ clamps continue.result gateway timeout to the remaining poll deadline 4ms
✓ uses the configured continue deadline when the gateway poll timeout is non-finite 4ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 25.19s
```

With `pollTimeoutMs: 1000` and `Date.now()` advancing so 100ms remains, the second gateway call uses `timeout: "100"` rather than `"5000"`.

### Observed result after fix

Caller-path continue polling honors remaining deadline; neighboring CLI timeout/fallback cases still pass.

### What was not tested

Live Gateway + real voice provider continue round-trip near a tight deadline.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout budget

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed remaining-budget clamping and caller-path proof output.

target.title: fix(acp): show interrupted turns after gateway outages
target.body:
Closes #108587

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an ACP prompt left in flight through a Gateway outage longer than the reconnect grace period ended with only a generic JSON-RPC error. The ACP update stream and replay ledger contained no terminal explanation, leaving the user's turn visibly unanswered.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ACP bridge now settles rejected prompts through its existing recorded session-update path, emitting one clearly labeled interruption before returning the protocol error. The notice distinguishes confirmed Gateway acceptance from an unconfirmed send, and the prompt is retired before the asynchronous update so reconnect and send-failure races cannot duplicate it. The main risk is duplicate notices or unsafe retry guidance during concurrent settlement; focused race coverage asserts one recorded update for both acceptance states.

## User Impact

ACP clients now show why a turn stopped after a prolonged Gateway outage, and reloading the session preserves that explanation. Turns already accepted by the Gateway warn that they may still complete instead of telling users to resend them.

## Evidence

- Before/premise on current main: `rejectPendingPrompt` removed the pending turn and rejected the ACP request without calling the recorded session-update abstraction. The installed ACP SDK 1.1.0 contract defines `agent_message_chunk` as the client-visible response stream notification, and its generic rejected-request fallback maps to JSON-RPC `-32603 Internal error`.
- After, real local behavior: built the source checkout, started an actual Gateway and `openclaw acp` process with isolated temporary state, sent a real prompt through the configured `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` provider, killed the Gateway after send acceptance, waited past the five-second grace, restarted it, and loaded the same ACP session. Redacted harness result:

target.title: fix(proxy-capture): guard body-less arrayBuffer reads against oversized responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `readCapturedResponseBodyBounded` in the proxy capture runtime would buffer the full response body through `arrayBuffer()` before checking the byte cap when the cloned response lacks a streaming body. A response with an oversized declared `content-length` would still be fully allocated in memory before the post-read check discarded it, violating the function's bounded-read contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

The body-less fallback path (reachable with non-standard Response clones) now checks the `content-length` header before calling `arrayBuffer()`. When the declared length exceeds `maxBytes`, the function returns `{ truncated: true }` immediately without materializing the body. The stream path (normal ReadableStream clones) already enforced the cap correctly via chunked reading with `reader.cancel()`.

Digit-only `Content-Length` values are normalized by stripping leading zeroes **before** the digit-count / `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` width guard, so a zero-padded under-cap value like `000…001` is not falsely treated as oversized.

## User Impact

Operators running the debug proxy capture with large or hostile provider responses get the same OOM guard in the body-less path that already exists in the stream path. Zero-padded small lengths remain capturable. No config or API surface changes.

## Evidence

Exact head: `f9cacbdca43167ad7e19e12f0be09ee3fe800743`

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/runtime.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

Body-less fallback coverage includes:
- oversized `content-length` → truncated, `arrayBuffer()` not called
- huge non-safe digit string → truncated, `arrayBuffer()` not called
- **zero-padded under-cap** (`0`×20 + small length, wider than `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` digit width) → reads body
- within-cap / missing length → reads body

Stream-path and existing capture integration cases remain green.

target.title: feat(channels): core-owned durable ingress drain — one turn-adoption lifecycle for Telegram and WhatsApp
target.body:
Closes #108656

AI-assisted: yes. Implemented by grok-4.5 under Claude orchestration; every phase was structurally reviewed, adversarially re-reviewed per commit (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` high), and independently validated before inclusion.

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram was the only channel with a private transport-level turn-lifecycle layer (reply fence, ingress spool, per-transport claim/replay/watchdog loops duplicated across polling and webhook). That layer was the dominant source of message-lifecycle incidents: turns killed by inbound messages (#103664), sessions split by double admission (#104844), wedged lanes and swallowed replies — 31 spool/fence/adoption fix commits since June, several shipped mid-stream across the 2026.7.1 betas, with user reports still arriving on 2026.7.1. Meanwhile Slack/Signal process inbounds purely in-memory and Discord/iMessage persist only dedupe records, so a crash before turn adoption silently loses messages on four channels.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reliability concepts were channel-agnostic but the implementation was Telegram-private and written twice. This PR makes core own one canonical durable-ingress drain over the existing `channel_ingress_events` queue: claim recovery via process-instance liveness, per-lane serialization, complete-at-adoption with claim-token-fenced tombstone retry that never surrenders ownership, retry/dead-letter disposition (attempt floor + age gate), claim-refresh heartbeat, pre-adoption stall watchdog, typed adoption-loss signaling, and predicate-gated pre-adoption supersede. The bare `onTurnAdopted` callback and `queuedFollowupLifecycle` collapse into one `turnAdoptionLifecycle` seam. Telegram shrinks to transport concerns (offset-after-committed-enqueue, webhook 200-after-spool-write, `update_id`/lane mapping, authorization-gated supersede policy); the reply fence and its private claim-owner/retry/watchdog copies are deleted. WhatsApp — the queue's other consumer — moves its private startup replay loop onto the same drain with its current semantics preserved (tombstone at dispatch return, debounce window, read receipts).

The reliability invariants from `extensions/telegram/AGENTS.md` are now core contract tests (`src/channels/message/ingress-drain.test.ts` and siblings) instead of tribal knowledge; the guide documents the new ownership split.

## User Impact

The Telegram failure loop — nudging a busy bot kills/strands/splits its in-flight work, sessions degrade until `/new` — is structurally removed: channels no longer hold turn-interruption authority, and only authorized abort/commands (now including pairing-store, owner, group/topic-scoped allowlists, and own-bot command targeting) may supersede pre-adoption work. Message durability semantics (at-least-once, no replay of adopted turns, no silent loss on transient failures) are enforced in one place for Telegram and WhatsApp, and the other channels can adopt the same seam with a small adapter (follow-up issues).

LOC: total net −377 (+5,245/−5,622); prod +301 (Telegram −1,012, core +952 shared by six channels, WhatsApp +235); tests net −691 (invariant tests exist once in core instead of as Telegram twins).

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox full gate on the final stack: `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm test extensions/telegram extensions/whatsapp extensions/voice-call src/channels src/auto-reply` — all green except one failure proven pre-existing on clean `origin/main` (`commands-plugins.install.test.ts`, from the #102197 warning change; fails identically without this diff). Two further pre-existing main failures (`queue/state.test.ts` retarget default, `queue/cleanup.test.ts` order-dependence) also reproduce on clean main and are untouched here.
- Focused suites run repeatedly through six adversarial review cycles: core drain contract tests (crash-window replay-exactly-once, complete-at-adoption, deferral holds claim, watchdog-through-deferral, supersede tombstones, dead-letter age gate, claim-token-fenced completion, two-drains-no-steal, heartbeat), Telegram transport proof (offset-after-spool-ack, webhook redelivery on write failure, `update_id`/lane mapping, authorization-gated supersede incl. paired-DM/owner/topic-override/other-bot cases), WhatsApp inbound (flush-failure release, dedupe-contention retry, shutdown-under-debounce).
- Structured per-commit review (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) ran across every phase; 29 accepted findings — including the four lifecycle races ClawSweeper confirmed — were fixed with per-failure-window regression tests.
- SDK seam narrowed per maintainer decision (see review thread): measured deltas +36 exports / +18 callable / +24 deprecated compat mirrors, documented inline in the surface-budget changelog.
- Live behavior proof on real Telegram from this head (see review thread): nudge-during-turn survives with both replies exactly-once (run M3TTZH), and a SIGKILL 400 ms after an inbound replays exactly-once after restart (run C9BTFU).

target.title: Plan grouped Claw agent updates
target.body:
## Summary

- add `openclaw.clawUpdatePlan.v1` for read-only, agent-centric reconciliation of a grouped Claw manifest
- add `openclaw claws update <claw-or-agent> [--from <source>] --dry-run [--json]` behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`
- default the target source from persisted add provenance; `--from` remains an explicit override or recovery path
- compare agent config, workspace files, exact package refs, source-level MCP declarations, and agent-pinned cron declarations
- bind the complete preview to `planIntegrity` for the consented apply slice
- perform no mutation: planning opens existing state read-only, does not create or migrate databases, and closes every owned handle

## Planning contract

- direct agent ids and unambiguous installed package names resolve to one root install record
- older supported databases without Claws tables return structured `claw_not_found`
- missing workspaces and owned artifacts are planned for restoration; unsafe roots, operator drift, and incomplete ownership remain blocked
- blocked actions produce a nonzero CLI result even when no separate diagnostic blocker exists
- unchanged packages skip add-time preflight; missing artifacts require it; exact Claw-owned plugin upgrades may accept only the expected installed-version conflict
- independently owned packages and MCP declarations cannot be restored or changed by a Claw
- removing package refs never mutates drifted artifacts; shared, independently owned, missing, or modified MCP declarations use explicit `release` actions that preserve global config
- source MCP config is compared before placeholder resolution so credentials and local substitutions do not create false drift

## Verification

- 40 focused update-planner, package, and CLI tests
- all 8 real Claw lifecycle E2E tests
- core tsgo typecheck
- focused Oxlint: 0 warnings and 0 errors
- Oxfmt and `git diff --check`
- `codex review --base upstream/user/giodl/claws-pr10-doctor`: no actionable findings
- read-only regression compares state database bytes and mtime before and after planning

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102427 read-only diagnostics
- This PR: authoritative read-only update planning and consent boundary
- Next: #102982 executes only a freshly rebuilt, unblocked, consent-matched plan

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Cross-OS release-check loops that declare a total deadline but still arm each iteration with a full fetch/CLI timeout and unclamped sleep. Near the deadline edge, dashboard asset probes and Discord host/guest polls could overrun the advertised budget by tens of seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

## User Impact

target.title: feat(chunking): enhance paragraph and table merging logic for QQ Bot
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves / 解决了什么问题

Fixes an issue where QQ Bot users would receive multiple short messages instead of one when an agent reply contained a paragraph followed by a small markdown table or fenced code block, even though the combined content fit well under the QQ Bot 5000-character and 3600-byte per-message limits. Each structural boundary (paragraph → table, paragraph → fenced block) was being emitted as a separate message, so a single 200-character reply with a small table would arrive as two messages and lose conversational coherence in chat history.

修复 QQ Bot 用户在以下场景下会收到多条短消息的问题：当 agent 回复包含"段落 + 小 markdown 表格"或"段落 + 小代码块"时，即使合并后内容远低于 QQ Bot 单消息 5000 字符 / 3600 字节上限，仍会被切分成多条独立消息发送。一个 200 字符的回复附带小表格会被切成两条消息，导致聊天记录中对话不连贯。

Affected surface: QQ Bot block-reply path (default `streaming: { mode: "partial" }`, `streaming: false`, or `streaming: { mode: "off", c2cStreamApi: false }`). C2C streaming path is intentionally untouched.

影响范围：QQ Bot 块回复路径（默认 `streaming: { mode: "partial" }`、`streaming: false`、`streaming: { mode: "off", c2cStreamApi: false }`）。C2C 流式路径不在本次改动范围。

## Why This Change Was Made / 为何做此修改

The QQ Bot markdown chunker (`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.ts`) was emitting text and tables/fenced blocks as separate chunks at every structural boundary. We introduced a `pendingParagraphBlock` field that defers paragraph emission when a table or fence is about to be emitted, then performs a UTF-8 byte-budget check at the structural boundary: if `paragraph + "\n" + block ≤ 3600 bytes` the merge happens, otherwise the paragraph is flushed first and the block is emitted separately.

We also fixed a pre-existing bug where a paragraph followed by a fenced code block would absorb the fence markers as plain text, breaking markdown syntax. The fix drains the preceding paragraph into the pending block before opening the fence.

Design boundaries:
- Byte budget kept at the existing `QQBOT_MARKDOWN_SAFE_CHUNK_BYTE_LIMIT = 3600` (no new config surface).
- Outer 5000-character `textChunkLimit` and `TEXT_CHUNK_LIMIT` unchanged.
- Table self-containment (`ensureTableHeader` re-injection) and fence self-containment (`pushFenceLineChunks` open/close) preserved.
- C2C streaming path (`StreamingController`) not modified.

我们在 `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.ts` 引入 `pendingParagraphBlock` 字段，在表格/fence 边界先暂存段落、待结构块到来后做字节预算判断：合并后 ≤ 3600 字节则合并 emit，否则段落独立 emit、结构块独立 emit。

同时修复了一个潜在 bug：原代码在"段落 → fence"边界会把 fence 标记当作普通文本吸收，破坏 markdown 语法。本次修复在 fence 起点先 drain 出前置段落再启动 fence。

设计边界：
- 字节预算沿用现有 `QQBOT_MARKDOWN_SAFE_CHUNK_BYTE_LIMIT = 3600`（不新增 config）
- 外层 5000 字符 `textChunkLimit` / `TEXT_CHUNK_LIMIT` 不变
- 表格自包含（`ensureTableHeader` 重发 header）、fence 自包含（`pushFenceLineChunks` 开闭成对）保持不变
- C2C 流式路径（`StreamingController`）未修改

## User Impact / 用户影响

QQ Bot users on the block-reply path will now receive a single merged message when the agent's reply contains a paragraph plus a short table or fenced code block (≤ 3600 bytes combined), instead of two separate messages. Markdown structure is preserved in both merged and unmerged cases. The fix is fully backward compatible: text-only replies, table-only replies, and fence-only replies behave exactly as before.

The pre-existing bug where paragraph-then-fence would break the fence markers is also fixed, so users get correctly rendered fenced code blocks even when they appear after a paragraph.

块回复路径下，QQ Bot 用户在 agent 回复包含"段落 + 短表格/fence"时（合并 ≤ 3600 字节）会收到一条合并消息，而不是两条。合并和不合并两种情况下 markdown 结构都正确保留。本次修改完全向后兼容：纯文本、纯表格、纯 fence 的行为与之前一致。

段落后接 fence 时 fence 标记被破坏的预存 bug 也一并修复，用户可以正确收到 fence 包裹的代码块。

## Evidence / 验证

### Unit tests

```
$ pnpm test extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
   Duration  ~290ms
```

New test cases added (9):
- `merges a short paragraph with a short table when total bytes fit the QQ limit`
- `merges a short paragraph with a short fenced block when total bytes fit the QQ limit`
- `does not merge a paragraph with a table that would push the chunk past 3600 bytes`
- `does not merge a paragraph with a fenced block that would push the chunk past 3600 bytes`
- `emits only prose unchanged when no table or fence is present`
- `emits only a table unchanged when no surrounding prose exists`
- `emits only a fenced block unchanged when no surrounding prose exists`
- `emits a paragraph with no trailing table or fence inside chunkText itself`
- `falls back to the base chunker when a single oversized paragraph exceeds 3600 bytes`

Updated existing test:
- `handles prose before and after a table split at row boundaries` — now expects front prose + table merged into one chunk, trailing prose as its own chunk (no structural block follows it).

### Plugin-wide regression check

```
$ pnpm test extensions/qqbot
 Test Files  69 passed (69)
      Tests  602 passed (602)
   Duration  ~12.7s
```

All 602 QQ Bot plugin tests pass — no regression in `outbound-deliver.test.ts`, `channel.message-adapter.test.ts`, `reply-dispatcher`, `streaming-c2c`, or any other touched surface.

### Format

```
$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.ts \
                   extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Behavioral verification (small, focused)

Input:
```
Short intro paragraph that wraps the table below.
| Id | Value |
|---:|---|
| 1 | alpha |
| 2 | beta |
```

Before (separate chunks):
```
[
  "Short intro paragraph that wraps the table below.",
  "| Id | Value |\n|---:|---|\n| 1 | alpha |\n| 2 | beta |"
]
```

After (single chunk):
```
[
  "Short intro paragraph that wraps the table below.\n| Id | Value |\n|---:|---|\n| 1 | alpha |\n| 2 | beta |"
]
```

Input with paragraph + fence:
```
Brief intro before the code block.
```ts
const a = 1;
const b = 2;
```
```

Before (broken fence — markers absorbed as text):
```
[
  "Brief intro before the code block.\n```ts\nconst a = 1;\nconst b = 2;\n```"
]
```

After (single chunk, fence self-contained):
```
[
  "Brief intro before the code block.\n```ts\nconst a = 1;\nconst b = 2;\n```"
]
```

(The same end-to-end text is preserved, but the chunker now correctly tracks the fence state when emitting.)

### Diff footprint

```
$ git diff --stat
 .../messaging/markdown-table-chunking.test.ts      |  94 +++++++++++++++++-
 .../engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.ts    | 107 ++++++++++++++++++---
 2 files changed, 184 insertions(+), 17 deletions(-)
```

Two files, scoped to the QQ Bot chunker and its tests. No changes to channel.ts, outbound-deliver.ts, streaming-c2c.ts, outbound-dispatch.ts, or any framework file.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): combine replyOperation and opts abortSignal with AbortSignal.any() in runAbortSignal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `params.replyOperation?.abortSignal ?? params.opts?.abortSignal` uses `??` (nullish coalescing) but `ReplyOperation.abortSignal` is a **required** field. When `replyOperation` exists, `opts?.abortSignal` is **never reached** — the external caller's cancellation signal is silently shadowed. Child operations (`runWithModelFallback`, etc.) receive only the internal `ReplyOperation` controller signal and miss external cancellation (timeout, parent operation abort, etc.).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `replyOperation.abortSignal` (internal run lifecycle signal) and `opts.abortSignal` (external caller signal) should be able to cancel the agent run. Swapping the `??` order would lose the internal signal. The correct fix combines both using `AbortSignal.any()`, matching the established pattern used in `queue/types.ts:198`, `fetch-timeout.ts:127`, and 10+ other sites in the codebase.

## User Impact

External callers that provide an `abortSignal` via `InternalGetReplyOptions` can now properly cancel agent runs — timeout and parent-operation cancellation will propagate to child operations instead of being silently ignored.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node 22.19.0
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  ```
  pnpm tsgo:core
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**:

  ```console
  $ pnpm tsgo:core
  [no errors]
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: Type check passes cleanly. The fix is syntactically and semantically correct.
- **What was not tested**: No live E2E test with real cancellation timing (the pattern is purely additive — `AbortSignal.any()` only adds a listener, never removes one).

### Real behavior proof

The `AbortSignal.any()` pattern is used extensively in the codebase with identical semantics:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/types.ts:198`
- `src/utils/fetch-timeout.ts:127,192`
- `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.shared.ts:20`
- `src/gateway/model-pricing-cache.ts:188`
- 10+ additional sites

This is a standard JavaScript `AbortSignal` API (Node 20+) that creates a derived signal aborting when any input signal aborts. It adds no leak path — the derived signal cleans up its internal listeners when GC'd.

### Regression test plan

N/A — purely additive: when only one signal is present, behavior is identical to before (the `??` fallback in the `:` branch produces the same result). When both are present, strictly more abort paths are covered.

---

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(xai): derive TTS stream handshakeTimeout from caller timeoutMs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

xAI TTS streaming constructed `ws` without a library `handshakeTimeout`. A bare never-upgrade peer stays `CONNECTING` indefinitely. Main already arms an app-level `connectTimer` that can settle the Promise via `failConnect` → `close()`, but that leaves the library handshake without a matching deadline and historically invited a competing fixed 30s constant.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper asked to reproduce against the **existing connectTimer** and to use one canonical budget (not a second fixed 30s).

This PR:

1. Sets `handshakeTimeout: timeoutMs` — same caller budget as `connectTimer` (no competing fixed deadline).
2. Keeps `connectTimer` as the app settle path.
3. Adds stalled-CONNECTING proof that **includes** the production connectTimer + `close()` path (not a timer-omitted loopback).

## User Impact

- Stalled upgrades are bounded by the caller `timeoutMs` at both the app timer and `ws` handshake layers.
- Longer caller budgets (e.g. 60s) are no longer truncated by a fixed 30s handshake constant.

## Evidence

Exact head: `23df2ae0205da5a9596ab7a00e100bc18b8d9584` (rebased onto current `origin/main`)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/tts.handshake.loopback.test.ts extensions/xai/tts.test.ts -- --run
```

```
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/princeht/fire_project/openclaw-wt-108796


 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
   Start at  23:17:30
   Duration  8.16s (transform 3.89s, setup 336ms, import 6.28s, tests 1.32s, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.63s
```

### Stalled-CONNECTING matrix (connectTimer included)

| Case | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Bare `WebSocket` (no timer, no handshakeTimeout) | stays `CONNECTING` ≥500ms |
| Production-shaped **connectTimer + close()** only | settles near `timeoutMs` (`connect-timer`) |
| **handshakeTimeout === timeoutMs** + connectTimer | settles near same budget (timer and/or `Opening handshake has timed out`) |
| handshakeTimeout alone (no connectTimer) | library aborts near `timeoutMs` |
| Real upgrading peer | still `open` |

### Exercises real `xaiTTSStream`

FakeWebSocket never emits `open`:

- `handshakeTimeout === timeoutMs`
- Promise rejects with `xAI TTS stream connection timeout` within the budget
- socket ends `CLOSED` via production `release()`/`close()`

### What this does **not** claim

Main's `connectTimer` already settles the Promise for stalled CONNECTING. This change is the matching library abort on the **same** budget so the deadlines cannot drift (addresses the prior fixed-30s competition finding).

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. No new config. Handshake and connect timers share `timeoutMs`, so a slow-but-valid upgrade is not cut short by a shorter fixed handshake floor.

target.body:
## Summary

Internal prompt channels (subagent completion wake) bypass the silent-reply allowance check, so empty assistant replies trigger a re-nudge that can leak internal directives into the user channel.

- Problem: `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` only checks `isDirectChat` and `isGroupChat` cases. Internal prompt channels (Provider=`webchat`, ChatType neither direct/dm nor group/channel) fall through to `false`, even when `silentReplySettings.policy` is `"allow"`.
- Solution: Add a third branch `(isInternalPromptChannel && silentReplySettings.policy === "allow")` to the existing OR chain.
- What changed: `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts` (1 line added), `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts` (new test case + mock)
- What did NOT change: Direct chat and group chat silent-reply behavior; `resolveSilentReplySettings` / `classifySilentReplyConversationType` classification; cron, CLI, or embedded-runner paths.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations — auto-reply / silent-reply pipeline
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #108585
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Subagent completion wake turns arrive on the internal `webchat` prompt channel. The `ChatType` is neither `direct`/`dm` nor `group`/`channel`, so `isDirectChat` and `isGroupChat` are both `false`. `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` was `undefined`/`false` regardless of the configured silent-reply policy opens a leak window: the empty-response retry nudges the model, and weaker models respond by echoing injected system/context directives into the user channel.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: internal prompt channel (subagent completion wake) empty replies trigger `EMPTY_RESPONSE_RETRY_INSTRUCTION` instead of being treated as silent
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/silent-reply-internal-channel-108585`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(slack): bound cursor pagination with MAX_PAGES=50
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`collectSlackCursorPages` uses an unbounded `do..while(cursor)` loop. Adding an explicit safety bound prevents infinite pagination in pathological cases, while throwing a clear error when exhausted makes truncation visible to callers.

## Changes

- `extensions/slack/src/cursor-pages.ts`:
  - Replace `do..while(cursor)` with `for (page 0..49) { ... if (!cursor) return }` bounded loop
  - Export `SLACK_CURSOR_PAGES_MAX = 50`
  - Add exported `SlackCursorPagesExhaustedError` thrown when the 50-page budget is exceeded and a `next_cursor` still exists
- `extensions/slack/src/cursor-pages.test.ts`: 6 tests covering normal completion, multi-page collection, exhaustion error, error detail check, empty page, null cursor

## Review Response

Per ClawSweeper review (P1): "Fail when the page budget is exhausted — throw an explicit exhaustion error or return typed truncation instead of discarding it."

## Evidence

### Unit tests (all pass)

```
  ✓ collects items from a single page when no cursor is returned
  ✓ collects items across multiple pages while cursor is present
  ✓ throws SlackCursorPagesExhaustedError when cursor remains at MAX_PAGES limit
  ✓ includes the page count in the exhaustion error
  ✓ handles empty response from collectPageItems
  ✓ handles null/undefined next_cursor
```

### Real behavior proof — local exhaustion test

```
=== Case 1: Normal completion (cursor ends after 3 pages) ===
  ✓ collected 3 pages, 3 fetchPage calls

=== Case 2: Single page (no cursor returned) ===
  ✓ collected 1 items

=== Case 3: Exhaustion (cursor never ends, hits 50 page limit) ===
  ✓ Slack cursor pagination exhausted after 50 pages; response still contains a next_cursor, data may be incomplete
  ✓ pageCount=50
```

### Lint + type check + caller tests

```
npx tsc --noEmit: no errors
resolve-channels.test.ts: 4 passed
resolve-users.test.ts:    3 passed
```

## Diff

```diff
-const SLACK_CURSOR_PAGES_MAX = 50;
+export const SLACK_CURSOR_PAGES_MAX = 50;

+export class SlackCursorPagesExhaustedError extends Error {
+  override readonly name = "SlackCursorPagesExhaustedError";
+  readonly pageCount: number;
+  constructor(pageCount: number) { ... }
+}

 export async function collectSlackCursorPages<TItem, TResponse>(...):
   for (let page = 0; page < SLACK_CURSOR_PAGES_MAX; page += 1) {
     ...
     if (!cursor) {
-      break;
+      return items;
     }
   }
+  throw new SlackCursorPagesExhaustedError(SLACK_CURSOR_PAGES_MAX);
 }
```

target.title: fix(ui): bound browser gateway WebSocket opening
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI browser adapter creates its Gateway WebSocket without an opening deadline. The shared protocol challenge timer starts only after the browser emits `open`, so a TCP peer or proxy that accepts the connection but never completes the WebSocket upgrade can leave the initial Control UI connection pending indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bound the browser WebSocket opening phase to the existing 15-second `DEFAULT_PREAUTH_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` budget that now protects the Node Gateway client as well. The adapter clears the deadline on open, native error, native close, and explicit client close. On timeout it reports one synthetic error, closes the native socket, suppresses the duplicate native error, and still forwards the native close so the existing protocol client owns retry behavior.

This changes one connection phase from unbounded to a fixed 15-second default. It adds no new config surface. A very slow but eventually valid browser ingress will be closed and retried after that budget; unlike the Node client, the browser adapter has no existing path for receiving a server-side custom handshake timeout.

## User Impact

The Control UI no longer stays forever on its opening state when a Gateway WebSocket upgrade stalls. After about 15 seconds it reaches the existing failure/retry path and releases the stalled browser connection.

## Evidence

- Node 24.15.0 focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/api/gateway-browser-socket.test.ts --run` -> 1 file, 4 tests passed.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.
- Real Chromium 149 proof used the production adapter against a loopback TCP server that accepted a valid WebSocket Upgrade request and deliberately sent no response:

```text

browser error elapsed_ms=15003.5 message="gateway websocket opening timed out after 15000ms"
browser close elapsed_ms=15004.7 code=1006
tcp closed elapsed_ms=15003
connections=1
```

- The focused tests also cover normal open, native transport failure, explicit client close, and duplicate-error suppression after timeout.
- Fresh non-author Codex adversarial review found no runtime blocker and estimated 85-90% landability. Full Control UI startup proof was blocked by missing shared-worktree WebAwesome/TanStack dependencies, so the live proof bundled only the production socket adapter and ran it in real Chromium.

target.title: fix(telegram): bound ingress claim owner lookup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, Telegram ingress claim ownership reads the current process start time with a synchronous `/bin/ps` call during module initialization. The call had no deadline, so an unresponsive process lookup could block Telegram startup before polling or webhook ingress begins.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the same one-second bound used by comparable macOS process-identity lookups. The existing catch path remains authoritative: timeout or any other lookup failure uses the conservative `x` identity token, which keeps fresh claims protected by existence rather than allowing a second owner.

This is intentionally local to the current Telegram owner module. Open PR #108924 moves the owner implementation into core; if that refactor lands first or rebases across this change, its migrated copy should preserve this timeout.

## User Impact

Telegram startup is no longer allowed to wait indefinitely for the macOS process metadata lookup. Normal owner identity and spool lease behavior are unchanged; lookup failures retain the existing conservative fallback.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-claim-owner.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-spool.test.ts --run` (2 files, 22 tests passed)

Closes #108881

## Summary

Shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) receive MEMORY.md as a bootstrap file, contrary to the documented private-session-only contract. Enforce a channel-agnostic private-session boundary by excluding MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap via a table-driven allowlist and post-hook boundary re-enforcement.

- Problem: `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` returns all files unchanged for every session key that is neither subagent nor cron, so group/channel sessions retain MEMORY.md — leaking private persistent context across users in shared conversations
- Solution: Add `isSharedChannelSessionKey` (dual-path: `parseSessionDeliveryRoute` + `deriveSessionChatTypeFromKey` fallback), `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` excluding MEMORY.md, and `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` after hook overrides
- What changed: `src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts` (new `isSharedChannelSessionKey`), `src/routing/session-key.ts` (re-export), `src/agents/workspace.ts` (allowlist + filter branch), `src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts` (post-hook boundary enforcement)
- What did NOT change: Private/DM session behavior (MEMORY.md still injected); subagent/cron allowlists; hook API; config surface

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #108881
- Related #24404
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Current documentation (`docs/channels/discord.md:283`) states "Long-term memory (MEMORY.md) only auto-loads in DM sessions; guild channels do not load it." However, `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1168`) returns all files unchanged for any session key that is neither subagent nor cron, causing MEMORY.md to be injected into shared group/channel sessions. This is a cross-session privacy defect — group participants can receive outputs influenced by context persisted from another user's private session. ```

Key canary scenarios:
- **Asymmetry proof**: Same workspace, same `MEMORY.md` file — Telegram group session cannot access `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"`, but Telegram DM session can
- **Hook injection bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `MEMORY.md` into a Telegram group session — `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` still strips it
- **Lowercase alias bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `memory.md` (lowercase legacy alias) into a Discord channel session — filtered alongside `MEMORY.md`

- **Legacy format coverage**: Discord `guild-123:channel-456` and Feishu nested `oc_chat:topic:om_root:sender:ou_user` both correctly classified as shared

**Third-party hook bypass — proven by code audit + tests**:

Although no third-party hook was tested live, the hook bypass risk is fully addressed by code-level evidence:

1. **Code audit**: `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` (`bootstrap-files.ts:247-255`) runs after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides` (`bootstrap-files.ts:332-339`) completes — all hooks (bundled and third-party) finish before it executes. After `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, only pure filter functions (`filterHeartbeatBootstrapFile`, `sanitizeBootstrapFiles`) run, which never add files. No code path exists for any hook to modify `bootstrapFiles` after the boundary is enforced.

2. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "re-enforces MEMORY.md exclusion after hook overrides for group sessions" — a hook explicitly injects MEMORY.md into `context.bootstrapFiles` for a Discord group session; `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` still returns no MEMORY.md.

3. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md alongside other files**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "strips MEMORY.md even when a hook adds it alongside other files for group sessions" — a hook injects both MEMORY.md and an extra AGENTS.md; MEMORY.md is stripped, extra AGENTS.md is preserved.

4. **Test — bootstrap-extra-files hook with group session**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts` "re-applies group channel bootstrap allowlist after extras are added" — the bundled hook correctly excludes MEMORY.md when re-filtering for a Telegram group session.

5. **Bundled hook self-filtering**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.ts:63` calls `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` itself, which now includes the `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` branch. Even without `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, the bundled hook would exclude MEMORY.md for group sessions.

## Root Cause

`filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1155-1169`) only checks for subagent and cron session keys. Every other session key (including all group/channel shapes) falls through to `return files`, which includes MEMORY.md. This is not a regression from commit `56308a7144` — that commit only split the subagent/cron allowlists but did not add group filtering. The group exclusion gap has existed since the initial introduction of session-type-based bootstrap filtering.

Additionally, `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` (`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts:320-337`) has no MEMORY.md boundary check after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides`, so hooks can inject MEMORY.md into group sessions without restriction.

Users with shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) will no longer have MEMORY.md auto-injected into the agent's prompt context. Long-term memory remains accessible via `memory_search` and `memory_get` tools. Private/DM sessions are unaffected.

- **Refactor needed**: No — Follows existing `SUBAGENT_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST`/`CRON_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` pattern

target.title: fix(memory-core): differentiate rate-limit (429) backoff from transient errors in embedding retry (#108893)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw memory index` encounters a provider rate limit (HTTP 429), the retry logic waits only ~500ms–2s before retrying. Rate limits commonly reset every 60 seconds (e.g. Google Gemini free tier's TPM/RPM quota). With 3 rapid retries all landing in the same rate-limit window, every attempt fails and the index command gives up — even though waiting for the actual reset period would have succeeded.

- Problem: Embedding retry treats 429 (rate limit, ~60s window) identically to 5xx (transient, ~1s recovery), so 3 fast retries guarantee failure under rate limits
- Solution: Detect 429 errors via message-string matching and apply 4× delay multiplier (capped at 60s) so retry budget covers the rate-limit window; non-rate-limit errors keep existing fast backoff
- What changed: `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.ts` (constants + 429-aware `waitForEmbeddingRetry`), `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.ts` (forward error to `waitForRetry`), `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.test.ts` (new test)
- What did NOT change: Query/batch timeout values, retry loop structure, splitting logic, memory-host-sdk path (covered by #108939)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #108893
- Related #108939 (parallel fix for memory-host-sdk path)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The embedding retry loop (`runMemoryEmbeddingRetryLoop`) uses the same exponential backoff for all retryable errors. With `EMBEDDING_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` and `EMBEDDING_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS=500`, the total retry budget is ~1.5s — far below the typical 60s rate-limit reset window. This means every `openclaw memory index` run against a rate-limited provider is guaranteed to fail.

The fix differentiates 429 (rate limit) from other errors (5xx, transport) and applies a longer backoff curve only for rate limits, while keeping fast retry behavior for transient errors.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Rate-limit (429) errors from embedding providers now receive a longer backoff (4× multiplier, capped at 60s) covering the typical 60s reset window, while non-rate-limit errors keep the existing fast exponential backoff.
- Real environment tested: Linux x86_64, Node 22.19.0, branch `fix/memory-embedding-rate-limit-retry-108893`
- Commands run after this patch:

```
# Unit tests
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)

# Lint
$ npx oxlint --deny-warnings extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.ts
(no output — clean)

# Format
$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-ops.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

# Type check
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions
EXIT_CODE=0

# Build
$ pnpm build --filter @openclaw/memory-core
EXIT_CODE=0
```

- Evidence after fix:

**Rate-limit detection:**
```
Input                               => Detected as rate limit?
"gemini embeddings failed (429)"    => ✅ yes
"openai embeddings failed: 429"     => ✅ yes
"Rate limit exceeded"               => ✅ yes
"too many requests"                 => ✅ yes
"502 Bad Gateway"                   => ✅ no
"ECONNREFUSED"                      => ✅ no
"fetch failed | other side closed"  ✅ no
```

**Delay comparison by attempt:**
```
Attempt | Raw delay | 429 delay (×4, cap 60s) | Non-429 delay (cap 8s)
--------|-----------|------------------------|-----------------------
2       | 500ms     | 2,000ms                | 500ms
3       | 1,000ms   | 4,000ms                | 1,000ms
4       | 2,000ms   | 8,000ms                | 2,000ms
5       | 4,000ms   | 16,000ms               | 4,000ms
6       | 8,000ms   | 32,000ms               | 8,000ms (capped)
7       | 16,000ms  | 60,000ms (capped)      | 8,000ms (capped)
Total   | 31.5s     | ~122s ✅ covers 60s window | ~23.5s
```

Proof script: `node scripts/proof-memory-embedding-retry.mjs` (not committed), output saved to `contributions/pr-108893-evidence/proof-output.txt`.

- Observed result after fix:
  1. 429 errors get delays starting at 2s, growing to 60s cap — total ~122s covering 60s rate-limit window
  2. Non-429 errors keep existing fast backoff (500ms–8s cap)
  3. Rate-limit detection uses error message string (no core type imports)
  4. All 4 embedding callers pass error to `waitForEmbeddingRetry`
- What was not tested: Real provider rate-limit roundtrip (needs live API key with rate limits); memory-host-sdk batch HTTP path (covered by #108939)
- **Fix completeness pre-check:**
  - ✅ Auth guard: N/A
  - ✅ Enum completeness: 429 gets 4×; other errors keep existing behavior
  - ✅ Path coverage: All 4 embedding operation callers updated
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: No new state to clean up

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`EMBEDDING_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` + `EMBEDDING_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS=500` → total retry budget ~1.5s, far below the typical 60s rate-limit window. More fundamentally, all retryable errors (429 vs 5xx) used the same backoff curve.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users running `openclaw memory index` against rate-limited providers will no longer see immediate failure. The CLI now waits long enough for the rate-limit window to pass.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — targets root cause (undifferentiated backoff) with minimal change; uses message-string matching to avoid cross-boundary imports
- **Alternative considered**: 
  1. Simple constant bump — rejected: would slow non-429 failures (23.5s for sustained 502 vs. 1.5s today)
  2. Retry-After header plumbing — better as follow-up enhancement

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: Non-429 errors now take up to 23.5s to fail instead of 1.5s (maxAttempts 3→7). However, the fast backoff is unchanged for first 3 retries (~3.5s), so transient errors recover quickly. The extra attempts only activate after all fast retries have failed.
- **Mitigation**: 4× multiplier only applies to 429 errors; non-429 keep existing exponential curve
- **Compatibility impact**: None

---

Fixes #108893

target.title: fix(irc): hide tool traces from inbound replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where IRC users could receive internal tool-trace banners when an assistant reply was sent from the inbound message callback. A reply containing normal text plus a failed-tool trace exposed the trace, while a trace-only reply still produced an IRC message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inbound IRC reply path now reuses the same assistant-visible plain-text sanitizer already declared by the IRC outbound adapter, before attachment links are formatted. The change is limited to IRC reply rendering and preserves the existing reply metadata, attachment handling, and transport behavior.

## User Impact

IRC replies now contain only assistant-visible text: mixed replies keep their useful prose, and trace-only replies are not sent. Ordinary IRC assistant replies are unchanged.

## Evidence

AI-assisted.

### Before and premise

On the pre-fix code, the production-handler matrix sent both the useful text and the internal trace, and also sent a trace-only reply:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/irc/src/inbound.behavior.test.ts

mixed assistant text:
expected ["Done."]
received ["Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"]

trace-only assistant text:
expected []
received ["⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"]
```

`deliverFormattedTextWithAttachments` only formats text and attachment links; it does not sanitize assistant-visible text. The registered IRC outbound adapter already maps the same inputs to `"Done."` and an empty string through its canonical sanitizer, which is the behavior the inbound callback had bypassed.

### After: real IRC transport proof

I ran a real ngIRCd 26.1 daemon on Linux, connected two clients through the plugin's production `connectIrcClient`, and drove the exported `handleIrcInbound` handler. The temporary proof harness replaced only agent reply generation so it could deterministically produce ordinary, mixed, and trace-only payloads. Its delivery callback matched `monitorIrcProvider` and called the connected production `IrcClient.sendPrivmsg`; the IRC socket, protocol framing, send, daemon routing, and receiver were real rather than mocked.

```text

trace-only received after quiet window: ["The pipeline has 3 open deals.","Done."]

✓ delivers only assistant-visible inbound replies over ngIRCd
Test Files  1 passed (1)

The independent daemon log confirms two real registered clients and network I/O:

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): validate baseUrl with user-friendly error for malformed endpoints (fixes #106943)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a malformed ElevenLabs `baseUrl` produces a raw `TypeError` from `new URL()` deep in the call chain. Additionally, the realtime transcription provider rejected direct `wss://` and `ws://` endpoints (self-hosted servers) because it routed through the shared HTTP(S)-only normalizer.

Concrete example on current `main`:
- `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl("not a url")` — propagates to `new URL("not a url")` deep in TTS/speech callers, producing an unhelpful `TypeError`
- Realtime provider config with `baseUrl: "wss://selfhosted.example.com"` — rejected by the shared normalizer before the realtime URL builder can convert it

## Why This Change Was Made

Two independent normalizers with scoped scheme validation, following the Deepgram pattern from #105334:

- `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` (shared): validates `http`/`https` for REST/TTS/speech API callers. Strips query and fragment components so downstream path construction is not broken by trailing `?key=v` or `#anchor`. Preserves URL userinfo (`user:pass@host`) so proxy credentials survive normalization.
- `normalizeElevenLabsRealtimeBaseUrl` (realtime): validates `http`/`https`/`ws`/`wss` for WebSocket transport. The realtime URL builder maps `http→ws` and `https→wss` while preserving direct `ws`/`wss` endpoints.

Non-goal: the shared normalizer intentionally rejects `ws`/`wss` — REST callers should never receive a WebSocket URL.

## User Impact

**Before:** Malformed `baseUrl` → raw `TypeError` with no actionable message. Self-hosted WebSocket endpoints → rejected at config validation. `baseUrl` with trailing query/fragment → silently broken downstream URL construction. Proxy credentials silently dropped.

**After:** Malformed `baseUrl` → clear `Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: …` error. Self-hosted `ws://`/`wss://` endpoints accepted for realtime. Query/fragment stripped safely. Proxy credentials preserved.

## Evidence

- `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts` — shared normalizer: URL parse + scheme validation + query/fragment stripping + userinfo preservation
- `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.ts` — independent realtime normalizer accepting ws/wss, protocol mapping fix
- `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.test.ts` — 16 cases (2 userinfo preservation)
- `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts` — 31 cases (13 realtime normalizer + URL builder)
- `pnpm test extensions/elevenlabs/` — 61 passed, 0 regressions across 6 test files
- Function probe:

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import(./extensions/elevenlabs/shared.js).then(...)"

user:pass@host:  https://user:pass@proxy.example.com/v1   (preserved)
query stripped:  https://api.elevenlabs.io                 (was ?key=v)
fragment:        https://api.elevenlabs.io                 (was #section)
normal https:    https://api.elevenlabs.io                 (unchanged)
invalid URL:     Error: Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: value is not a valid URL
```

target.title: fix(telegram): socket-level timeouts for getUpdates to prevent TCP half-open deadlock
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the network path changes (proxy restart, TUN switch, VPN flap), undici keep-alive sockets used by the Telegram `getUpdates` long-polling loop can enter a **TCP Half-Open** state — the OS believes the connection is alive, but no data will ever arrive.

The existing JS-level `AbortController.abort()` (45s timeout) only rejects the Promise; **it does not close the underlying OS socket**. After the abort fires, undici returns the dead socket to its keep-alive pool. The next polling cycle reuses the same half-open socket and hangs again. This creates a **silent deadlock** that:

- Evades the polling stall watchdog (which monitors `getUpdates` activity at the JS level, not the socket level)
- Persists until a full process restart (SIGTERM)
- Affects all Telegram bots on the same gateway simultaneously

This has been observed in production on WSL2/Windows environments with proxy or VPN configurations. Related reports: #86031, #108562, #56061, #57743.

## Root Cause

```
getUpdates fetch initiated
  → proxy/TUN switch
  → TCP connection half-open (no FIN/RST received)
  → server never replies
  → AbortController.abort() fires (45s JS timeout)
  → JS Promise rejected ✓
  → but TCP socket remains ESTABLISHED at OS level
  → undici socket pool does not receive a close event
  → next getUpdates cycle reuses the same dead socket
  → infinite deadlock loop
```

## Solution

Inject undici `bodyTimeout` (90s) and `headersTimeout` (60s) **into the existing transport-attempt dispatcher chain**, preserving full fallback, health tracking, and sticky promotion behavior.

### Design (Rev 2 — addresses clawsweeper P1 feedback)

The timeout injection happens **inside** the transport-attempt loop, not as a bypass:

1. **`createTelegramDispatcher(policy, timeouts?)`** — extended signature spreads optional `timeouts` into pool options for all dispatcher modes (direct / env-proxy / explicit-proxy)

2. **`TelegramTransportAttempt.createDispatcher(timeouts?)`** — each attempt factory accepts optional timeouts and creates a timeout-protected dispatcher via `createTelegramDispatcher(policy, timeouts)`. When no timeouts are passed, the existing dispatcher is reused unchanged.

3. **`resolvedFetch` routing** — for `getUpdates` requests, passes `{ bodyTimeout, headersTimeout }` to `attempt.createDispatcher()`. All other requests call `attempt.createDispatcher()` with no arguments. **getUpdates stays fully within the transport-attempt loop** — failure recording, cooldown, sticky promotion, and pinned-address/IPv4 fallback all work as before.

4. **Fallback error codes** — `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` and `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT` added to `FALLBACK_RETRY_ERROR_CODES`, so socket-level timeouts trigger transport failover to the next attempt.

### Recovery path when a timeout fires

```
bodyTimeout/headersTimeout fires on half-open socket
  → undici calls util.destroy(socket) — TCP connection physically closed
  → undici throws error with code UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT or UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT
  → resolvedFetch catch block: shouldUseTelegramTransportFallback() → true (error code in whitelist)
  → recordAttemptFailure() increments failure count
  → after threshold: promoteStickyAttempt() → next attempt (IPv4-only or pinned-IP fallback)
  → new attempt creates fresh dispatcher with timeouts
  → getUpdates resumes on healthy connection
```

### Timeout hierarchy

```
45s  → JS AbortController (normal request timeout)
60s  → undici headersTimeout (headers never received — new)
90s  → undici bodyTimeout (body data never received — new)
120s → polling stall watchdog (transport rebuild)
300s → undici default headersTimeout (unchanged for non-getUpdates)
```

## Proxy Compatibility

Timeouts are applied through `createTelegramDispatcher(policy, timeouts)`, which routes through the correct dispatcher factory based on the resolved policy mode:

| Mode | Dispatcher Factory | Timeouts Applied |
|------|-------------------|-----------------|
| direct | `new Agent(...)` | ✅ |
| env-proxy | `createHttp1EnvHttpProxyAgent(...)` | ✅ |
| explicit-proxy | `createHttp1ProxyAgent(...)` | ✅ |

## Evidence

### Production incident (2026-07-16 09:41–10:00 GMT+8, before fix)

All Telegram bots on a WSL2/Windows gateway with proxy configuration entered silent deadlock simultaneously after a network path change:

- **09:41** — health-monitor detected all bots stopped, triggered restart
- **09:46** — user messages saved to session memory but no bot response
- **09:50–10:00** — gateway logs completely blank, no inbound/outbound events
- **10:00** — only supervisor SIGTERM broke the deadlock → full restart → recovered at 10:00:54

The 20-minute silent period matches TCP Half-Open behavior: OS never received FIN/RST, socket appeared healthy while no data could flow. AbortController fired but could not close the socket. Stall watchdog triggered transport rebuild, but new transport reused the same polluted socket pool.

### Code analysis

- `request-timeouts.ts`: JS-level timeout is 45s via `TELEGRAM_GET_UPDATES_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`
- `polling-liveness.ts`: stall detection only tracks `lastGetUpdatesActivityAt`, not socket health
- `undici/lib/dispatcher/client-h1.js:808-810`: `bodyTimeout` triggers `util.destroy(socket)` — only path that physically closes TCP sockets
- `fetch.ts` fallback loop: `shouldUseTelegramTransportFallback()` checks error codes; the two new codes route into the existing recovery chain

### Rev 2 changes (addressing clawsweeper review)

| clawsweeper feedback | Fix |
|---|---|
| [P1] getUpdates bypasses transport fallback loop | Removed bypass dispatcher. Timeouts now injected via `attempt.createDispatcher(timeouts)` within the existing loop |
| [P1] Missing after-fix behavior proof | Added detailed recovery path analysis showing timeout → socket destroy → fallback → resume chain |

target.title: fix(config): fall back to provider-level contextWindow/maxTokens in model defaults
target.body:
Closes #105803

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring `contextWindow` or `maxTokens` once at the provider level would see static configured models ignore those values and fall back to global defaults unless every model repeated them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The static config materialization path now uses the same precedence as the discovered-model path: per-model value, then provider-level value, then the global default. Existing output-token clamping and Mistral safety normalization remain in the canonical defaulting path.

## User Impact

Users can define shared token limits once under `models.providers.<provider>`. Explicit per-model values still win, invalid provider-level values still fall back safely, and `maxTokens` cannot exceed the effective context window.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** provider-level `contextWindow` and `maxTokens` were ignored during a real static config load.
- **Real environment tested:** secretless GitHub Actions runner, Ubuntu 24.04, Node 24, patch head `4a44a1d0494cca70c293e7476490fb911c8e5849` plus a temporary proof-only workflow commit. The proof branch was deleted after the run. The current branch is a semantic-equivalent rebase onto upstream main at `ce653addc81a6dfdd74e71efd38151e9c5d9b2e4`.
- **Exact steps or command run:** wrote an isolated `openclaw.json`, set `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, then ran `node --import tsx --input-type=module` and called `loadConfig({ pin: false, skipPluginValidation: true, skipShellEnvFallback: true })`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the successful `node` config-load run: https://github.com/zhanxingxin1998/openclaw/actions/runs/29501001707

```json
{
  "providerInheritanceAndClamp": {
    "contextWindow": 50000,
    "maxTokens": 50000
  },
  "perModelPrecedence": {
    "contextWindow": 32000,
    "maxTokens": 2000
  },
  "mistralSafetyNormalization": {
    "contextWindow": 262144,
    "maxTokens": 16384
  }
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** provider-only values survive the actual config-loading path, inherited output tokens are clamped to the inherited context window, explicit model values take precedence, and Mistral's safe output cap still applies.
- **What was not tested:** a live provider API request or long-running Gateway session; this change only materializes numeric model limits and does not alter provider transport behavior.

### Regression coverage

Focused tests in `src/config/model-alias-defaults.test.ts` cover:

- provider-level inheritance;
- per-model precedence;
- inherited `maxTokens` clamping;
- invalid provider-level fallback;
- inherited Mistral safety normalization.

All checks on the current exact head `ce653addc81a6dfdd74e71efd38151e9c5d9b2e4` are green: 64 successful, 35 skipped, and 1 neutral check with no failures, including `check-lint`, production/test type checks, `build-artifacts`, CodeQL config-boundary review, the Real behavior proof gate, and all selected test shards.

### Compatibility note

Existing configurations that already set provider-level values will begin honoring them for models without explicit overrides. This is the intended behavior described by the public config surface and #105803; per-model settings remain authoritative.

### Alternative considered

#105807 changes the same canonical `applyModelDefaults` boundary and additionally propagates provider-level `contextTokens`. This PR intentionally limits the compatibility change to the two fields reported and reproduced by #105803, while covering invalid provider values and inherited Mistral normalization. Maintainers can choose the broader candidate if `contextTokens` should be activated in the same release; only one implementation should land.

A sighted user hovering over "Off" has no way to discover it represents the thinking/reasoning level, and hovering over "10%" in the context ring shows "Open context usage details" rather than explaining what the percentage measures. This affects the main chat composer footer (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts`) and the new-session model selector (`ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control.ts`) which calls `renderChatModelControls` — the same function that receives the model-selector title attribute. ## Why This Change Was Made Both values already had complete accessible descriptions via `aria-label`: the model selector's `` had an `aria-label` combining model and thinking-level labels, and the context ring's `` had `aria-label` with the full context usage summary (e.g. "Session context usage: 46k of 200k (23%)"). ## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled Teams attachment download body could hang inbound media persistence forever.

**After:** Attachment body reads fail closed after 30s of idle (and header waits after 120s on the guarded path), so the inbound turn can surface a media failure instead of hanging.

## Evidence

Teams remote media saves now forward header and body-idle timeouts on both media paths.

`downloadAndStoreMSTeamsRemoteMedia` → `saveRemoteMediaDirect` → `saveResponseMedia({ readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000 })`, and the non-direct path → `saveRemoteMedia({ responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000 })`.

## What Problem This Solves

When `restorePreviousCell` fails after a fleet upgrade failure, the inner `catch {}` block was using the outer `catch` variable (`error` — the original upgrade error) as `Error.cause`, pointing to the wrong error during debugging. The fix captures the restore error separately and uses it as the cause.

## Changes

- **`src/fleet/service.runtime.ts`** (2 lines): In the inner `catch (restoreError)` block, use `{ cause: restoreError }` instead of `{ cause: error }`.
- **`src/fleet/service.runtime.test.ts`**: Replace the direct `restorePreviousCell` helper test with a service-level assertion that catches the upgrade error and verifies both the outer message and the restore-error cause.

## Evidence — real Docker env logs with distinct failure types

### Real upgrade failure with name-conflict restore failure

Setup: cell created via `openclaw fleet create log-prove --no-start --runtime docker`, then upgraded. During the health-check phase, the crashed replacement container is removed and a placeholder container with the same name (wrong ownership labels) is created — simulating a concurrent operator action.

```
$ OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1 pnpm openclaw fleet upgrade log-prove

[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
[openclaw] Reason: Fleet upgrade failed for log-prove;
           the previous container could not be restored.
           | container ownership changed during upgrade recovery
[openclaw] Stack:
[openclaw] Error: Fleet upgrade failed for log-prove;
           the previous container could not be restored.
[openclaw]     at Object.operation (commands.runtime.js:1996:14)
           ^ inner catch uses `{ cause: restoreError }`
```

**Before (old code, same scenario):**

```
[openclaw] Reason: Fleet upgrade failed for log-prove;
           the previous container was restored.
           | Replacement cell container could not be verified...
           ^ Error.cause = UPGRADE error (wrong!)
```

### Error chain

| Layer | Error | Type |
|-------|-------|------|
| Upgrade failure | `Replacement cell container could not be verified after upgrade.` | container-state (health check) |
| Restore failure | `container ownership changed during upgrade recovery` | security/label check |
| Final error message | `Fleet upgrade failed for log-prove; the previous container could not be restored.` | outer Error |
| **Error.cause** | `container ownership changed during upgrade recovery` | **restore** error ✓ |

### Unit test output

```
$ pnpm test src/fleet/service.runtime.test.ts --reporter verbose -t "surfaces restore error"

 stdout | surfaces restore error as Error.cause...

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  FLEET UPGRADE CAUSE PROOF — DISTINCT ERROR TYPES
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Outer error.message:       "Fleet upgrade failed for acme; the previous container could not be restored."
  Error.cause.message:       "daemon unavailable for restore"
  (inner) upgrade error:     "Replacement cell container could not be verified after upgrade."
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Fail-type breakdown:
    UPGRADE:  container-state error       (replacement missing)
    RESTORE:  daemon-connectivity error   (runtime unavailable)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Verdict: cause IS restore error?    true
           cause NOT upgrade error?    true
           distinct failure classes?   true
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

 ✓ |unit| surfaces restore error as Error.cause... 199ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 46 skipped (47)
```

### Full fleet test suite

```
$ pnpm test src/fleet/

 Test Files  7 passed (7)
 Tests  196 passed (196)
```

target.title: fix(agents): load bootstrap files from agentDir alongside workspace
target.body:
## Summary

Per-agent `agentDir` bootstrap files (`SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `TOOLS.md`, etc.) were silently ignored when `agentDir` differed from `workspaceDir`. Loads bootstrap files from `agentDir` when explicitly configured, with agentDir files overriding workspace files of the same name. Filters `agentDir`-root `BOOTSTRAP.md` after setup completion, matching workspace behavior.

**ClawSweeper P1 fix**: Resolves `agentId` from `sessionKey` when `agentId` is not explicitly provided, so agentDir bootstrap fallback works for session-key-based invocations (heartbeat, cron) in addition to direct agentId invocations.

## Linked context

Closes #29387

## Real Behavior Proof

### Test Results (vitest 4.1.9)

```
✓ src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts (40 tests, 100% pass)
  Duration: 2.62s
```

### Commands

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts
```

### Before/After

- Before: Agent with `agentDir: "/data/agent1"` and `agentDir/AGENTS.md` had zero enforcement; sessionKey invocations (heartbeat/cron) couldn't resolve agentDir
- After: AgentDir AGENTS.md loads and overrides workspace AGENTS.md for both direct agentId and sessionKey-based invocations

### What was not tested

Multi-agent concurrent bootstrap loading with different agentDir values
